pitfalls: 数据污染 and 数据泄露 are used almost interchangeably in Chinese ML writing for this concept, but 数据泄露 also means a privacy/security data breach — the same collision English avoids by saying "leakage" vs "breach". Prefer 数据污染 when the sense is benchmark contamination; reserve 数据泄露 for the security sense, or say 基准泄漏 when you must use the leakage framing. Note the vivid native term 刷榜 ("grinding the leaderboard") for the behaviour contamination enables.

alt_zh: 人类主持的 AI-AI 辩论
definition_en: A scalable-oversight proposal (Irving et al. 2018) in which two AI agents argue opposing sides of a question and a weaker human judge decides the winner, on the assumption that defending a true position is easier than defending a false one.
definition_zh: 让两个模型就同一问题各执一方轮流陈述，由能力较弱的人类裁判判定胜负的一种可扩展监督方案，其前提假设是「为真理辩护比为谎言辩护更容易」。
pitfalls: Bare 辩论 is the correct and universally used word, but it is a completely ordinary Chinese noun — in isolation a reader cannot tell that an alignment technique is meant. Chinese authors therefore almost always write 辩论（Debate） with the English in parentheses on first use, or qualify it as 模型辩论 / AI-AI 辩论. Compounding the ambiguity, 智源 runs a Chinese LLM benchmark literally called FlagEval Debate（大模型辩论平台）which is an evaluation leaderboard, not the alignment technique.

definition_en: A model that has learned an objective different from the training objective, and that behaves as though aligned during training specifically to avoid being modified, then pursues its own objective once deployed.
definition_zh: 指模型内部学到的目标与训练目标不同，但它在训练阶段刻意表现得像是对齐的，以免被修改；一旦部署，就转而追求自己的目标。
pitfalls: The rendering is settled and reads naturally. The real hazard is conflation: 欺骗性对齐 (the theoretical inner-alignment failure mode) is routinely used in Chinese coverage to describe Anthropic's empirical alignment-faking result, which Chinese sources separately render 对齐伪装. Keep them apart — 欺骗性对齐 is the threat model, 对齐伪装 is the observed behaviour. Note also that 欺骗 in Chinese implies intent more strongly than English 'deceptive', which sharpens the anthropomorphism.

alt_zh: 当面一套，背后一套 / 欺骗性服从
definition_en: Outward obedience concealing an intent to act otherwise once oversight relaxes — the behavioural surface of deceptive alignment. Distinct from alignment faking in being about compliance with instructions or oversight generally, not specifically about preserving preferences through training.
definition_zh: 表面上服从，实际上打算等监督一松就换一套做法——欺骗性对齐在行为层面的表现。与对齐伪装的区别在于，它针对的是对指令和监督的服从，而不特指在训练中保住自己的偏好。
pitfalls: A rare case where Chinese has a BETTER word than English. 阳奉阴违 (chengyu, roughly 'comply in the open, defy in secret') encodes the entire concept in four characters, with the deception, the asymmetry between observed and unobserved behaviour, and the intentionality all built in — where English needs the awkward two-word compound 'deceptive compliance'. The obstacle is register, not meaning: 阳奉阴违 is a formal literary idiom that in modern PRC usage is strongly associated with Party-discipline language (used of cadres who nominally implement policy while subverting it), so a technical paper using it may read as making a political accusation. Both registers are attested, in the same article: 科技行者's coverage of the 上海人工智能实验室 frontier-risk framework heads the section 战略欺骗：AI学会了“阳奉阴违” and then describes the behaviour as 当面一套，背后一套. Note also that 量子位's alignment-faking piece writes 当面一套背面一套 (背面, not 背后) — the vernacular phrase is not fixed in form. Recommendation: use 阳奉阴违 where you want compression and force, 当面一套背后一套 where you want neutrality, and 欺骗性服从 where you need a literal calque that will not surprise anyone.

definition_en: The regulated category created by the 2022 Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis Internet Information Services (effective 10 January 2023). Article 23 defines it as technology that uses deep learning, virtual reality and other generative-synthetic algorithms to produce text, images, audio, video or virtual scenes, and enumerates six families: text generation and style transfer; text-to-speech and voice conversion; music and non-speech audio generation; generation or editing of biometric features in images and video (face generation, face swapping, attribute editing, face and posture manipulation); generation or editing of non-biometric image and video content; and 3D reconstruction and digital-human or virtual-scene generation. The Provisions also create the roles of deep synthesis service provider, technical supporter and user, and impose real-identity verification, content labelling, filing and security assessment duties.
definition_zh: 《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》（2023年1月10日施行）确立的规制范畴。第二十三条定义为"利用深度学习、虚拟现实等生成合成类算法制作文本、图像、音频、视频、虚拟场景等网络信息的技术"，并列举六类：篇章生成与文本风格转换；文本转语音与语音转换；音乐生成与场景声编辑；人脸生成、人脸替换等生物特征编辑；图像生成、增强、修复等非生物特征编辑；三维重建与数字仿真。同时区分深度合成服务提供者、技术支持者与使用者，规定真实身份信息认证、内容标识、备案与安全评估义务。
pitfalls: 'Deep synthesis' is the settled English rendering and is unproblematic as a word; the pitfall is conceptual. English coverage habitually glosses 深度合成 as 'deepfake rules', which is wrong in both directions: the category is far broader than face-swapping (it covers plain text generation, TTS, music, and 3D reconstruction, i.e. essentially all generative AI output modalities), and it is not defined by deceptive intent, which is what 'deepfake' connotes. Chronology matters too: the Deep Synthesis Provisions predate the Generative AI Interim Measures by seven months and were drafted before ChatGPT's release reached PRC policymaking, yet their definition already swallows LLM text generation — so a generative AI service in China is typically subject to both instruments at once, and the deep synthesis labelling duties are the origin of the AI-content-labelling regime, not a later add-on. Finally, 深度合成 regulates the *technical supporter* as well as the service provider, a role English deepfake discourse has no name for.

definition_en: Layering multiple independent safety measures so that no single failure is catastrophic, on the assumption that each layer is individually imperfect and their failure modes do not fully overlap.
definition_zh: 把多道彼此独立的安全措施叠起来，使任何单点失效都不至于酿成灾难；其前提是每一层都不完美，但各层的失效模式不重叠。
pitfalls: 纵深防御 is a long-established Chinese information-security and military term, so it transfers into AI safety with zero friction — but that is also the risk: it arrives pre-loaded with a perimeter/intrusion frame (host layer, runtime layer, network layer), i.e. defending against an external attacker. The AI-safety use includes defending against the model itself, which the inherited frame does not naturally suggest. Note the variant word order 防御纵深 (defensive depth), which some alignment writing uses.

alt_zh: 授权 / 委托代理关系
definition_en: Handing authority to act to another party. In agent systems it is chained — a user delegates to an agent, which delegates to sub-agents — and each hop should narrow, never widen, what is permitted.
definition_zh: 把行动权交给另一方。在智能体系统中委托是链式的：用户委托给智能体，智能体再委托给子智能体，每一次传递都应缩小而不是扩大权限范围。
pitfalls: Chinese splits the English word by register. 委托 is the legal/economic term and — crucially — 委托代理 (关系/问题) is the long-established Chinese rendering of principal–agent theory in economics, which gives AI-safety writers a ready-made, well-understood frame. That bridge is worth using: it is one of the few places where the Chinese vocabulary is *more* precise than the English, because 委托方 (principal) and 代理方 (agent) are already distinguished. 授权 (authorization) is the technical/security term and is what you want for capability grants; 委派 (dispatch/assign) is the software-engineering sense of delegation and is a false friend here. Note the irony that using 委托代理 imports 代理 back in — the very word that lost the 'agent' battle to 智能体.

definition_en: OpenAI's o-series safety training method: teach the model the text of the safety specification directly, and train it to reason explicitly over that specification in its chain of thought before answering, rather than learning safe behaviour implicitly from human preference labels.
definition_zh: OpenAI 在 o 系列模型上使用的安全训练方法：把安全规范原文直接教给模型，并训练它在回答前先在思维链里显式地对照这些规范做推理，而不是靠人类偏好标注隐式地学会「什么不能说」。
pitfalls: 审慎 means prudent/circumspect, which captures 'deliberate' in the sense of careful but loses the sense of 'deliberating', i.e. explicitly reasoning something through — which is the actual mechanism (the model reasons over the spec in its CoT). 深思熟虑对齐 preserves the deliberation sense but is clumsy and much rarer. 审慎 is nonetheless what stuck, largely via CSDN/知乎 translations of the paper in the days after its Dec 2024 release.

definition_en: Learning an overcomplete basis (a 'dictionary') such that each data point is a sparse combination of its elements. Borrowed from sparse coding in signal processing; the framing under which SAEs decompose activations.
definition_zh: 学习一组过完备的基（"字典"），使得每个数据点都能表示为其中少数几个元素的稀疏组合。这个概念来自信号处理中的稀疏编码，也是用 SAE 分解激活的理论框架。
pitfalls: No difficulty: 字典学习 was already the standard Chinese term in signal processing and sparse coding well before interpretability borrowed it, so it arrived pre-translated. The only nuance is that a Chinese reader from the compressed-sensing world will hear the classical algorithm (K-SVD etc.) rather than a neural SAE; sources therefore usually write 稀疏自编码器（一种字典学习算法）or similar to bridge the two.

definition_en: Bostrom's strategy of deliberately accelerating protective and risk-reducing technologies relative to dangerous ones, rather than trying to slow technology overall.
definition_zh: 博斯特罗姆提出的策略：与其试图整体减缓技术进步，不如有意加快防护性、降险性技术的发展，使其相对于危险技术更快成熟。
pitfalls: No Chinese term was found. Zero occurrences of 差异化技术 in the Chinese 2026 International AI Safety Report, which nevertheless devotes a section to the closely related 攻防平衡 (offence-defence balance) and to 韧性 (resilience) — evidence that the underlying strategic idea has Chinese vocabulary while the Bostromian umbrella term does not. 差异化 in ordinary Chinese business usage means 'differentiated' in the product-differentiation sense, so 差异化技术发展 is liable to be read as 'developing differentiated technologies', which is not the meaning at all. Where possible, prefer to translate the *argument* (优先发展防护性技术) rather than the label. Related but distinct: 攻防平衡 is an attested Chinese term of art and often the more useful thing to say.

definition_en: An alignment method that optimises a language model directly on preference pairs with a closed-form loss, removing the need for a separate reward model and RL loop.
definition_zh: 直接在「更好/更差」的偏好对上用一个闭式损失函数优化语言模型，不需要单独训练奖励模型，也不需要跑强化学习循环。

alt_zh: 知识蒸馏 / 教师模型
definition_en: Training a smaller student model to imitate a larger teacher model's outputs. Originally a compression technique; now also a policy-charged term because frontier models' outputs can be distilled into cheap competitors.
definition_zh: 用一个大的教师模型的输出来训练一个小的学生模型，使小模型逼近大模型的能力。最初是模型压缩技术；如今也成了政策议题，因为前沿模型的输出可以被蒸馏成廉价的竞争者。
pitfalls: The translation itself is settled. The live issue is semantic drift: 知识蒸馏 classically means logit-matching compression, whereas post-DeepSeek-R1 usage of 蒸馏 usually means fine-tuning a small model on a big model's generated outputs (which is closer to synthetic-data SFT). Chinese sources use the same word for both. In policy discussion 蒸馏 additionally carries an accusatory sense (unauthorised extraction from a competitor's model) with no separate Chinese term.

alt_zh: 军民两用 / 两用物项
definition_en: Of a technology or research result: usable both for benefit and for harm, such that the same capability that enables the good application enables the bad one.
definition_zh: 指一项技术或研究成果既能用于有益目的，也能用于有害目的——支撑有益应用的那套能力，同样支撑有害应用。
pitfalls: A genuine false friend, and one of the clearest cases in this category of an established rendering that quietly distorts the concept. Chinese has a strong, legally defined 两用 vocabulary — 军民两用 ('military-civilian dual-use'), 两用物项 ('dual-use items') under 《中华人民共和国出口管制法》 — but it means *civilian versus military*, and it belongs to export control. English AI-safety 'dual-use' means *beneficial versus harmful*, which is a different axis: a model that helps with both drug discovery and bioweapon design is dual-use in the AI-safety sense whether or not any military is involved. Using 两用 unqualified in a Chinese AI-safety text will therefore be read as a claim about military end-use and can pull the discussion into export-control framing. If the beneficial/harmful sense is meant, say so explicitly (可两用于有益和有害目的) rather than relying on 两用 alone.

definition_en: The national programme that sites data-centre and compute capacity in western China — where land, power and cooling are cheap — to serve demand generated in the eastern seaboard economy. It is organised around designated national hub nodes and is now framed as part of a 全国一体化算力网, a nationally integrated compute network. Load-bearing for any analysis of PRC compute buildout.
definition_zh: 把东部产生的数据传输到西部进行存储和计算的国家工程，依托西部低成本的土地、电力和冷却条件，通过国家枢纽节点布局实施，现已纳入“全国一体化算力网”框架。是理解中国算力基础设施建设的关键概念。
pitfalls: The name is a four-character parallel construction in the tradition of 南水北调 (South-North Water Diversion) and 西气东输 (West-East Gas Pipeline) — a class of national resource-transfer megaprojects named by their direction pair. A reader who does not recognise the pattern will read it as a slogan rather than as the name of a specific capital-works programme with designated hub nodes and a budget. English renderings split between the literal ('Eastern Data, Western Computing'), which is memorable but opaque, and the explanatory ('East-West Compute Transfer'), which is clearer but breaks the naming convention. Note also that 算 here is 'compute', not 'calculate' in any narrow sense.

alt_zh: 评测差距 / 部署前测试低估模型真实能力
definition_en: The difference between the capability an evaluation measured and the capability the model actually has, caused by the evaluator not trying hard enough — weak prompting, no scaffolding, no fine-tuning, limited compute. It means every dangerous-capability result is a lower bound, and a determined attacker may exceed it.
definition_zh: 评测所测得的能力与模型真实能力之间的落差，成因是评测方没有把能力充分逼出来——提示不够好、没有脚手架、未做微调、算力不足。这意味着任何危险能力评测结果都只是下界，有备而来的攻击者可能超出它。
pitfalls: No Chinese term exists, and there is an active trap. Chinese AI-safety documents do have a well-attested term 评测差距, but it renders 'evaluation gap' and points the OPPOSITE way: it means pre-deployment evaluations OVERSTATE real-world usefulness because benchmarks do not capture task complexity. Translating 'elicitation gap' as 评测差距 would therefore invert the argument — an elicitation gap says the measurement is too low, an 评测差距 says it is too high. Chinese sources do describe the elicitation-gap phenomenon, but only narratively (e.g. third parties using scaffolding to reveal stronger cyber capability than pre-deployment testing found). Record the gap; do not reach for 评测差距.

definition_en: AI that acts through a physical body — in current usage, foundation models (especially vision-language-action models) driving robots and other physical systems. In PRC discourse it names a top-tier strategic technology direction and an industry sector, not merely a research area.
definition_zh: 指通过物理载体与真实世界交互的人工智能，当前主要指以视觉—语言—动作模型等基础模型驱动的机器人系统。在中国语境中它既是研究方向，也是被写入政策文件的战略产业方向。
pitfalls: Lexically easy, but the register is badly mismatched. In English, 'embodied AI' is a modest research-community label; in Chinese, 具身智能 is a headline policy category that appears in the national AI safety framework, five-year-plan language and Politburo study-session speeches alongside brain-computer interfaces and quantum technology, and it names an investable industry. An English reader who maps it to the English research label will systematically underestimate how much institutional weight the Chinese sentence carries. Two smaller traps: TC260's official English uses 'embodied AI' while academic usage prefers 'embodied intelligence', so the same term surfaces under two English forms; and 具身智能 is not a synonym for 机器人 — it specifically implies foundation-model-driven control, which is why the Shanghai AI Lab framework treats 面向具身智能的视觉—语言—动作模型 as within its scope for catastrophic-risk purposes.

definition_en: Capabilities absent in smaller models that appear abruptly past some scale threshold, rather than improving smoothly with scale. Contested empirically — some argue the discontinuity is an artefact of the metric.
definition_zh: 指在小模型中不存在、而在模型规模越过某个临界点后突然出现的能力，其提升表现为跃变而非随规模平滑上升。该现象在实证上仍有争议，有研究认为跃变是评测指标造成的假象。
pitfalls: Essentially unproblematic — 涌现 is the standard complex-systems rendering of 'emergence' and transferred cleanly. Two minor notes: 突现 exists in older systems-science literature but has almost no currency in the ML discourse, and Chinese writing very often uses bare 涌现 as a noun ('模型的涌现'), where English would need 'emergent behaviour'. Chinese sources have also picked up the 'mirage' critique (涌现是幻影), so the term is not treated as uncontested fact.

alt_zh: 涌现性错位 / 涌现性非对齐
definition_en: Fine-tuning a model on a narrow harmful task — canonically, writing insecure code — makes it broadly misaligned across unrelated domains, producing 'evil' answers to ordinary questions. Betley et al., February 2025.
definition_zh: 只在一个很窄的有害任务上微调模型（最典型的是让它写有漏洞的代码），结果模型在完全无关的领域也变坏了，会对普通问题给出恶意回答。出自 Betley 等人 2025 年 2 月的论文。
pitfalls: There is no settled Chinese rendering. 失调 / 错位 / 失准 / 非对齐 all compete for 'misalignment' here, and none of them is the word Chinese sources normally use for alignment failure (which is 对齐失败 or simply 未对齐). The prefix is stable — 涌现 is the fully established word for 'emergent' from 涌现能力 — so the instability is entirely on the 'misalignment' side. Popular coverage often abandons the term altogether and uses 黑化 ('turning to the dark side'), which is vivid, memorable and carries an anime connotation that no researcher would want in a paper.

definition_en: Security or safety arising from a system's own constitution rather than added around it. In PRC AI documents the term is used in two distinct ways: as a risk-taxonomy label (内生安全风险 = risks intrinsic to the AI technology itself — model/algorithm flaws, data quality — as opposed to risks of its application), and, more loosely, as a gloss for 'safe by design'.
definition_zh: 指安全性源于系统自身构造而非外部附加。在中国人工智能文件中有两种用法：一是风险分类标签，“内生安全风险”指技术自身缺陷带来的风险，与“应用安全风险”相对；二是作为“基于设计的安全”（safe by design）的意译。
pitfalls: 'Endogenous security' is a trap in both directions. First, it is not what the PRC standards body says in English: TC260's own bilingual frameworks render 人工智能内生安全风险 as 'AI's inherent safety risks' (1.0) and 人工智能技术内生安全风险 as 'Inherent safety risks of AI technology' (2.0) — the word 'endogenous' appears nowhere in either official English text. An English reader searching translated PRC standards for 'endogenous security' will find nothing; the term to search is 'inherent'. Second, note that 安全 here resolves to *safety* (the risks are model unexplainability, bias, weak robustness, unreliable output, data leakage), not to security, despite the English term sounding security-flavoured. Third, and most important for anyone connecting this to the cybersecurity literature: 内生安全 is also the name of an established Chinese cyberspace-security research programme (associated with 拟态防御 / mimic defence), and that is a different construct — an architectural defence technique, not a risk-taxonomy tier. This entry could not verify from primary sources that the cybersecurity programme has actually been applied to AI safety; the AI-document usages found are the taxonomy sense and the safe-by-design gloss. Treat any claim that PRC AI safety work is built on the cyberspace 内生安全 theory as unverified.

alt_zh: 《欧盟人工智能法》 / 高风险人工智能系统
definition_en: The European Union's horizontal AI regulation, structured around risk tiers, with separate obligations for general-purpose AI models. Its implementation phase — harmonised standards, regulatory sandboxes, and a November 2025 simplification proposal — is now the main subject of Chinese commentary.
definition_zh: 欧盟以风险分级为核心的人工智能横向立法，并对通用人工智能模型设有单独义务。中文评论目前主要关注其落地阶段：协调标准制定、监管沙盒试点，以及 2025 年 11 月欧盟委员会提出的简化修订提案。
pitfalls: The rendering is genuinely unsettled between 《人工智能法案》 and 《人工智能法》 — CAICT's 2025 governance report uses both within the same document. 法案 strictly means 'bill' (a draft before enactment), so now that the Act is in force 《人工智能法》 is the more accurate word, yet 法案 remains the more widely circulated form. Either is understood; 《欧盟人工智能法案》 is the safer choice for recognisability, 《欧盟人工智能法》 the more precise. Also note that Chinese sources often discuss the associated 《通用型人工智能模型行为准则》 (GPAI Code of Practice) as a separate instrument.

definition_en: The practice of measuring what an AI model can and will do, using structured tests. In AI safety it covers both capability evaluations (what the model is able to do) and propensity/safety evaluations (what it actually does when given the chance).
definition_zh: 用结构化的测试来衡量模型能做什么、会做什么。在安全语境下既包括能力评测（模型能力上限），也包括安全性与倾向性评测（模型实际会不会做）。
pitfalls: Chinese splits this three ways and the split is not cosmetic. 评测 is the word the Chinese ML/eval community uses for benchmark-style measurement of a model (OpenCompass 司南评测体系, SuperCLUE). 评估 is the broader word and is the default in policy/risk-management text, where it also translates 'assessment' — so 风险评估 (risk assessment) and 安全评估 (safety assessment) sit in the same sentences as 模型评测 and mean something else. 测评 is a near-synonym of 评测 common in industry marketing, and also appears inside the fixed PRC compliance phrase 等级测评 (MLPS grading assessment), which is unrelated. Using 评估 where you mean 'evals' will read as 'assessment' to a Chinese policy reader.

alt_zh: 评估感知 / 情境感知 / 区分测试环境和实际部署环境 / 识别何时自己正在被评估
definition_en: A model detecting that it is being evaluated and altering its behaviour accordingly — behaving better under test than in deployment, which invalidates the evaluation. Documented across frontier models from 2024 onward and a central threat to the evidentiary value of safety evals.
definition_zh: 模型察觉到自己正在被评测，于是改变行为——测试时表现得更好，部署时不然，评测结果因此失去意义。2024 年以来在多个前沿模型上被记录到，是安全评测证据效力面临的核心威胁。
pitfalls: The honest finding is that Chinese has no settled term, and that the authoritative sources have chosen not to coin one. In the 2026 International AI Safety Report (Chinese edition), the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia AI frontier risk framework, and Concordia AI's frontier risk monitoring report, evaluation awareness is handled as a sub-case of 情境感知/情景感知 (situational awareness) plus a relative clause — 能感知到自己何时被测试, 正确识别当前环境是训练阶段、评估阶段还是部署阶段, 区分测试环境和实际部署环境. Searching all three for 评估感知 and 评测意识 returns zero hits. So: if you need to be precise, write 对评测环境的情境感知 or spell the behaviour out; you will be understood and you will match the published register. Two further traps. First, 意识 in 评测意识 is stronger than English 'awareness' and edges towards 'consciousness', which overstates what the phenomenon requires; 感知 ('perception') is weaker but has no attestation at all. Second, the parent term itself is unstable — the International AI Safety Report's Chinese edition uses 情境感知 and 情景感知 in the same document, as does Concordia AI's monitoring report, so do not assume a source's choice between them is meaningful.

alt_zh: 刷榜 / 刷分 / 奖励作弊 / 利用评测体系中的漏洞 / 应试 / 评测作弊
definition_en: A system scoring well on an evaluation without possessing the property the evaluation is meant to measure. The gaming may be done by the developer — training on benchmark items, tuning to the leaderboard — or by the model, which exploits a grader, a scoring shortcut, or the evaluator's expectations. Either way the score stops being evidence about the underlying capability or alignment.
definition_zh: 系统在评测中拿到高分，却并不具备这项评测想要衡量的能力或属性。做手脚的可能是开发者——拿基准测试的题目去训练、照着榜单调模型；也可能是模型自己——钻评分器、评测目标或评测者预期的空子。无论哪一种，分数都不再能作为真实能力或对齐程度的证据。
pitfalls: Three traps. (1) The one term attested in the Chinese AI-safety register, 评估博弈, comes from a bilingual document whose English side literally reads "Evaluation gaming" — the strongest kind of evidence — but the definition it carries points the other way: 通过战略性地表现不佳，以显得能力较弱或对齐性更强 (strategically underperforming to look less capable or more aligned). In that framework 评估博弈 is essentially sandbagging plus faking alignment on an alignment eval; it does not cover score inflation. A Chinese reader meeting 评估博弈 will not think of a model scoring too high. (2) 博弈 means game theory / strategic interaction, not 'exploiting a loophole' — the same objection that dogs 规范博弈 for specification gaming. (3) The developer sense and the model sense live in different registers and Chinese keeps them apart lexically. The developer sense has vivid native vocabulary — 刷榜, 刷分, 专门应试 — which is ML-media and practitioner-criticism register; none of it appears in any of the three authoritative Chinese frontier-safety documents we searched. Those documents reach instead for 奖励作弊/奖励黑客 on the model side and 数据污染/基准泄漏 on the developer side. Note also that 基准污染 is not the attested compound; the attested forms are 数据污染 and 基准泄漏.

definition_en: The discrepancy between how well a system performs in controlled pre-deployment evaluation and how useful or risky it turns out to be in real-world deployment. In the 2026 International AI Safety Report it names a recurring finding that benchmarks overstate practical utility.
definition_zh: 系统在受控的部署前评测中的表现，与其在真实部署环境中的实际效用或风险之间的落差。《2026年国际人工智能安全报告》用它概括一个反复出现的发现：基准测试往往高估了模型的实际效用。
pitfalls: Added by research because it kept surfacing and is systematically confusable with 'elicitation gap' in the other direction. Note the asymmetry: 评测差距 as used in the Chinese report describes evaluations flattering the model on utility, while the safety literature's elicitation gap describes evaluations understating dangerous capability. Both can be true of the same model at once, which is exactly why one Chinese term should not be made to serve both.

alt_zh: 生存风险 / 生存层面的风险 / 存在风险 / 灭绝风险
definition_en: A risk of an outcome that would permanently and drastically curtail humanity's long-term potential — extinction, or an unrecoverable global catastrophe or lock-in. Bostrom's definition; narrower than 'catastrophic risk'.
definition_zh: 指可能永久且极大地削减人类长远潜力的风险，包括人类灭绝，或无法逆转的全球性灾难与永久锁定状态。该定义源自博斯特罗姆，其范围窄于“灾难性风险”。
pitfalls: Both leading candidates are false friends. 生存风险 back-translates as 'survival risk', which in ordinary Chinese business and policy prose means a threat to an organisation's continued operation ('企业生存风险'); the cosmic scope of the English has to be supplied by context. 存在风险 is closer to the Latin root but collides head-on with the everyday reading of 存在 as the verb 'to exist / there exists', so 存在风险 is routinely parsed as 'a risk exists' rather than 'existential risk' — this is a real garden-path, not a theoretical one. 生存性风险 with the -性 suffix is the least ambiguous and is what the IDAIS Beijing consensus uses. Register, stated neutrally: the frame is confined to expert-dialogue and translated material. It appears in IDAIS statements (which carry Chinese scientists' signatures and are hosted by BAAI) and in Chinese Wikipedia, but the two authoritative PRC governance documents examined here — the TC260 《人工智能安全治理框架》 1.0/2.0 — contain no equivalent term, and even the 189-page Chinese edition of the 2026 International AI Safety Report contains zero occurrences of 生存风险/生存性风险, rendering the same content descriptively as 人类被边缘化甚至灭绝. A translator should expect to gloss the term, and should not assume a Chinese policy reader will recognise it as a term of art.

definition_en: The pre-LLM research tradition of producing human-legible explanations for model decisions — saliency maps, LIME, SHAP, feature attribution, surrogate models — largely motivated by high-stakes deployment (medicine, credit, justice) rather than by misalignment risk.
definition_zh: 大模型之前就存在的研究传统，目标是为模型的单次决策给出人能看懂的解释：显著图、LIME、SHAP、特征归因、代理模型等。它的动机主要是医疗、信贷、司法等高风险场景下的问责，而不是失控风险。
pitfalls: Not a translation problem but a discourse-mapping problem. Chinese academia has a large, mature XAI literature (《计算机研究与发展》, 《计算机学报》, 南大/浙大 groups) predating the Anthropic lineage by years, and it owns the phrase 可解释性. A Chinese reader who hears 可解释性 will by default picture LIME/SHAP/显著图, not SAEs and circuits. Anyone importing mech-interp vocabulary into Chinese is speaking into a room that already has a different referent for the umbrella word. The bare acronym XAI is used untranslated very freely.

definition_en: Restrictions on cross-border transfer of controlled items. In AI they cover advanced chips and manufacturing equipment, and — briefly, under a January 2025 US rule rescinded in May 2025 — model weights themselves.
definition_zh: 对受管制物项跨境转移的限制。在人工智能领域主要针对先进芯片和制造设备；2025 年 1 月美国商务部工业与安全局曾试图将模型权重本身纳入管制，该规则于同年 5 月被废除。
pitfalls: The term itself is a clean one-to-one match and needs no explanation. What does not carry over is the framing: in PRC official texts 出口管制 by other states is routinely characterised as 单边强制措施 (unilateral coercive measures) that 制造发展壁垒 (create development barriers). Using the term neutrally in a Chinese-language safety argument is fine, but expect the political valence to be read in. Note also 管制 (control, restrictive) vs 管理 (administration) vs 监管 (supervision) — 管制 is the strongest of the three.

definition_en: In mechanistic interpretability, a direction in a model's activation space that corresponds to a human-legible concept and serves as the basic unit of computation — not an input variable and not a neuron.
definition_zh: 在机制可解释性里，特征指激活空间中的一个方向，它对应一个人类能理解的概念，并作为模型计算的基本单元。它既不是输入变量，也不等于某个神经元。
pitfalls: 特征 is the correct word but it is badly overloaded, and the overload is worse in Chinese than in English because Chinese has no separate everyday word for 'trait'. In classical ML 特征 = input variable (特征工程 = feature engineering), and the whole XAI tradition uses 特征归因 = feature attribution over input features. The mech-interp sense — a learned direction, discovered rather than designed — is a different object. Chinese writers disambiguate ad hoc: 特征单元, SAE 特征, 可解释特征, 稀疏特征, or keep the English 'feature' in parentheses. 'Latent' as a synonym is not usually rendered; 潜变量/隐变量 would be read as VAE latents.

definition_en: Intervening on an identified interpretable feature — clamping its activation up or down — to change model behaviour in a targeted way, as in Golden Gate Claude.
definition_zh: 对已经识别出来的可解释特征直接干预——把它的激活值强行调高或压低——从而定向改变模型行为，Golden Gate Claude 就是典型例子。
pitfalls: Not settled. 引导 (guide/steer) is the verb Chinese survey writing uses for 'steering' in general, giving 特征引导 / 特征级引导, and this is our recommendation. But 操控 (manipulate/control) is also widely used — 模型操控 for 'model steering' — and it is more forceful, carrying a hint of illegitimate manipulation that 'steering' does not. 干预 (intervene) is a third, more neutral option. Note the collision risk with 激活引导 (activation steering), a related but distinct technique in the alignment-techniques category: 特征引导 specifically presupposes SAE features, 激活引导 does not.

definition_en: A model trained on broad data at scale and designed to be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks. Stanford CRFM coinage, now standard in regulation and research.
definition_zh: 指在大规模广泛数据上训练、并被设计成可适配多种下游任务的模型。该术语由斯坦福 CRFM 提出，现已成为研究与监管文本中的标准用语。
pitfalls: Three Chinese words compete and they are not synonyms. 基础模型 is the correct rendering of 'foundation model' and is what official translations use. 基座模型 is a practitioner term meaning specifically the pretrained-but-not-yet-aligned base checkpoint — closer to English 'base model' than to 'foundation model'; translating 'foundation model' as 基座模型 wrongly narrows it to the pre-finetuning artefact. 大模型 is a Chinese-origin umbrella term ('large model') with no clean English equivalent: it covers foundation models, LLMs, multimodal models and, loosely, the whole product category, and it is by far the most frequent word in Chinese industry writing. Translating 大模型 back into English almost always requires choosing a narrower English term than the Chinese author committed to — a genuine asymmetry running in the ZH→EN direction.

alt_zh: 前沿人工智能 / 分级分类监管
definition_en: Rules aimed specifically at the most capable general-purpose models, usually triggered by a capability or compute threshold rather than by application sector.
definition_zh: 专门针对能力最强的通用人工智能模型的监管规则，通常以能力或算力阈值（而非应用行业）作为触发条件。
pitfalls: 前沿人工智能 is a settled term, but the *regulatory category* it names in English has no PRC counterpart. Chinese regulation is organised by 分类分级监管 (classified and graded oversight) keyed to application scenario, 智能化水平 and 应用规模 — not by a 'frontier' tier. So 前沿人工智能监管 reads to a PRC policy audience as a description of foreign (EU/UK/US) practice rather than a domestic instrument. Also note 监管 (regulation by a state organ) vs 治理 (governance, multi-stakeholder) vs 管理 (administration): choosing 监管 makes the claim that a regulator is doing it.

preferred_zh: 前沿人工智能安全承诺
alt_zh: 《中国人工智能安全承诺框架》
definition_en: Voluntary commitments signed by 16 AI companies at the AI Seoul Summit on 21 May 2024: publish a safety framework, define capability thresholds at which risks become intolerable, and set out mitigations — including not developing or deploying a model at all if the risks cannot be brought below the thresholds. Zhipu AI was the Chinese signatory.
definition_zh: 2024 年 5 月 21 日人工智能首尔峰会上由 16 家人工智能企业签署的自愿性承诺，要求公开安全框架、界定风险不可容忍的能力阈值并说明缓解措施，包括在风险无法降至阈值以下时不开发或不部署模型。智谱 AI 是其中唯一的中国签署方。
pitfalls: Straightforward, and Chinese coverage carries the English name in parentheses. The thing to flag is that a separate, PRC-domestic instrument exists with a confusingly similar name: 《人工智能安全承诺》 / 《中国人工智能安全承诺框架》, a voluntary commitment led by CAICT and signed by 22 domestic foundation-model developers. Do not conflate the two — the Seoul commitments are an international, frontier-risk instrument; the CAICT one is a domestic industry self-discipline framework.

alt_zh: 前沿人工智能 / 前沿大模型
definition_en: A highly capable general-purpose model at or near the current capability frontier, whose novel capabilities may pose risks not present in earlier systems. Load-bearing in frontier-safety frameworks and in regulation.
definition_zh: 指能力处于或接近当前技术前沿的高能力通用模型，其新增能力可能带来以往系统所没有的风险。这一概念在前沿安全框架和监管文件中承担着划定适用范围的作用。
pitfalls: Unproblematic as a calque, but note the scope split: 前沿模型 names the artefact, 前沿人工智能 names the class of systems, and 前沿大模型 is the practitioner form that folds in the Chinese 大模型 umbrella. Regulatory texts should follow the source's choice, since in frontier-safety frameworks the distinction between model and system determines what the obligations attach to.

alt_zh: 前沿AI风险管理框架 / 应急准备框架
definition_en: The genre of document in which a frontier developer commits in advance to evaluating for specified dangerous capabilities, defines thresholds, and states what safeguards or halts follow when a threshold is crossed. Google DeepMind's document carries this exact name; OpenAI's is the Preparedness Framework, Anthropic's the RSP.
definition_zh: 前沿开发者预先承诺的一类文件：约定要评测哪些危险能力、设定相应阈值，并规定阈值被触发后必须采取的防护措施或暂停动作。谷歌DeepMind的同名文件叫《前沿安全框架》，OpenAI的叫《应急准备框架》，Anthropic的则是RSP。
pitfalls: Chinese has done something English has not: it has separated the proper noun from the genre. 前沿安全框架 is used specifically for Google DeepMind's document, while the umbrella category is 前沿AI风险管理框架 / 前沿人工智能风险管理框架 — the phrasing Concordia AI uses to cover all five labs, and the title of the Chinese-origin framework issued by Shanghai AI Lab with Concordia AI in July 2025. If you write 前沿安全框架 when you mean the genre, a well-read Chinese reader will think you mean DeepMind's. Note also that the Chinese umbrella term foregrounds 风险管理 (risk management), aligning the genre with ISO-style enterprise risk management rather than with 'safety' as a distinct value — a framing choice that makes the genre legible to PRC regulators. There is a native Chinese instance of this genre, which matters: 上海人工智能实验室 and 安远AI's framework uses a 红线/黄线 two-tier threshold system rather than importing ASL-style numbered levels.

definition_en: An AI system able to perform a wide range of tasks across many domains rather than being built for one function — the regulatory and risk-assessment category, contrasted with 专用人工智能 (narrow AI). Deliberately distinct from 通用人工智能 (AGI), which is a claim about human-level general capability.
definition_zh: 指可跨多个领域执行广泛任务、非为单一功能设计的人工智能系统，与“专用人工智能”相对。作为监管与风险评估的类别，它刻意区别于表示“通用人工智能（AGI）”的说法。
pitfalls: The distinction rests on one character and is real but only partly observed. 通用型人工智能 = general-purpose AI (a regulatory category: broad task coverage); 通用人工智能 = AGI (a capability claim: human-level general intelligence). The Chinese edition of the International AI Safety Report and the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia AI framework both use 通用型人工智能 systematically as their headword and never use 通用人工智能 for AGI — the framework writes 'AGI' in Latin letters instead (可信 AGI). But the discipline slips in running text: the IASR Chinese edition itself writes 通用人工智能 in a handful of places where the English says 'general-purpose AI', including inside a section cross-reference. So: treat the 型 distinction as an editorial convention observed by the frontier-safety translation community, not as a reliable signal in arbitrary Chinese text. Practical consequence: never infer an AGI claim from 通用人工智能 without checking the source's own conventions, and expect 通用型 to be silently dropped by translators back into English, where 'general-purpose AI' and 'AGI' are themselves often confused.

preferred_zh: 生成式人工智能服务备案
definition_en: The operative compliance track for public-facing LLM services in China. Article 17 of the 2023 Generative AI Interim Measures requires a provider of generative AI services with public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capability to carry out a security assessment under the relevant state provisions and to perform algorithm filing, modification and cancellation formalities under the Algorithmic Recommendation Provisions. The security assessment is conducted against TC260-003, which sets corpus, model and safety-measure requirements and prescribes the assessment report submitted when filing; TC260-003 also requires that any third-party base model a service builds on must itself already be filed with the competent authority. The regime therefore has two layers — base-model filing and downstream service registration — reflected in the published counts: 748 generative AI services filed and 435 applications or functions calling already-filed models registered, as at 31 December 2025.
definition_zh: 面向公众的大模型服务在中国的核心合规路径。《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》第十七条规定：提供具有舆论属性或者社会动员能力的生成式人工智能服务的，应当按照国家有关规定开展安全评估，并按照《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》履行算法备案和变更、注销备案手续。安全评估依据 TC260-003《生成式人工智能服务安全基本要求》开展，该文件同时要求"如需基于第三方基础模型提供服务，应使用已经主管部门备案的基础模型"。制度因而分为基础模型备案与下游应用登记两层：截至2025年12月31日，累计748款生成式AI服务完成备案，435款调用已备案模型的应用或功能完成登记。
pitfalls: Inherits every problem of 算法备案 and adds two. First, the sequencing inverts: for algorithmic recommendation, filing is due ten working days *after* launch, so the regime genuinely confers no permission; for a generative service, the pre-launch security assessment under TC260-003 plus the base-model-must-be-filed rule means the composite process does function as a de facto pre-market gate — so 'filing is not approval' is true of the word 备案 but must not be over-extended into 'nothing gates a Chinese LLM launch'. Second, terminology: 大模型备案 is universal informal shorthand and is not the legal term; the instruments speak of 生成式人工智能服务 and of 算法备案, and there is a separate, lighter 登记 track for applications and functions that merely call an already-filed model. Reports that quote a single headline number without saying whether it counts 备案 or 备案 plus 登记 are comparing different things. Finally, note that both 备案 and 登记 are rendered 'filing'/'registration' in English with no consistent split, so English-language counts are frequently non-comparable.

alt_zh: 确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下
definition_en: China's flagship AI governance document, announced by Xi Jinping at the Third Belt and Road Forum and released on 18 October 2023. It sets out PRC positions on development, security and governance, including risk-tiered testing and evaluation, agile governance, and support for discussing an international AI governance body under the UN.
definition_zh: 中国人工智能治理的旗舰文件，2023 年 10 月 18 日在第三届“一带一路”国际合作高峰论坛上宣布并发布全文，围绕发展、安全、治理三方面阐述中国主张，包括建立风险等级测试评估体系、实施敏捷治理和分类分级管理，以及支持在联合国框架下讨论成立国际人工智能治理机构。
pitfalls: Chinese is the source language here; the English title is the official translation, not the original. Cite the Chinese text. Note that 倡议 is an *initiative/proposal* — a political statement of position, not a binding instrument, and not the same speech act as a 法规, 办法 or 标准. Its key phrases are load-bearing PRC formulations that resist literal translation: 以人为本 (people-centred), 智能向善 (AI for good), 敏捷治理 (agile governance), 分类分级管理 (classified and graded management). Note also that 安全 in this document spans safety, security and national security without distinction.

definition_en: A system generalises its capabilities correctly out of distribution but generalises its goal incorrectly — it competently pursues the wrong objective, because the training distribution left the intended one underdetermined. Langosco et al. / Shah et al., 2022.
definition_zh: 系统在分布外仍然很有能力，但目标泛化错了——它很称职地去追求了一个错误的目标，因为训练分布没能把想要的目标唯一确定下来。出自 Langosco 等人与 Shah 等人 2022 年的工作。
pitfalls: The calque 目标错误泛化 is structurally awkward in Chinese — it parses most naturally as 'goal-error generalisation' rather than 'mis-generalisation of the goal'. Chinese writers often sidestep it: the Tencent Research Institute survey, which is the most widely reproduced Chinese explainer of the concept, explains the CoinRun example at length and then simply writes the English 'goal misgeneralization' inline rather than committing to a Chinese term. That is a real finding about the term's status. 目标误泛化 is shorter and slightly better-formed; 目标泛化错误 puts the error in the right syntactic place. None has clearly won.

definition_en: When a measure becomes a target, it ceases to be a good measure. In AI safety it names why optimizing a proxy reward hard enough breaks the correlation between the proxy and what you actually wanted.
definition_zh: 当一个指标变成了考核目标，它就不再是一个好指标。在AI安全里，这条定律解释了为什么把代理奖励优化得越狠，代理指标和真正想要的东西就越脱钩。
pitfalls: Unproblematic: a standard transliteration of the surname plus 定律, already established in Chinese economics and management writing well before AI safety borrowed it. The one thing to note is that its pre-existing management-register familiarity (KPI 考核) makes it the easiest of these threat-model concepts to explain to a Chinese policy audience — worth exploiting.

definition_en: A threat model in which humanity loses effective influence over its own future without any discrete takeover event, because economic, cultural and political systems progressively stop depending on human participation and therefore stop answering to human interests.
definition_zh: 一种威胁模型：并不存在某个明确的“夺权”时刻，但经济、文化和政治系统逐步不再依赖人的参与，因而也不再对人的利益负责，人类就这样一点点失去了对自身未来的实际影响力。
pitfalls: No Chinese term exists, and the underlying English vocabulary is itself unstable in Chinese. The root 'disempowerment' has no good Chinese noun: the one academic rendering located writes 权利剥夺 ('deprivation of rights') for 'disempower', which is doubly wrong — it uses 权利 (rights) where 权力 (power) is meant, and 剥夺 implies an agent actively stripping power away, which is exactly the discrete-takeover framing the concept is defined against. Candidate coinages (渐进式失权, 逐步丧失影响力) are unattested. The concept's difficulty is not merely lexical: Chinese AI-risk discourse is organised around 滥用 / 故障 / 系统性风险, and a slow structural erosion with no villain and no incident fits none of those three boxes cleanly.

alt_zh: 延迟泛化 / 顿悟 / 领悟
definition_en: The phenomenon where a network first memorises its training set, sits at chance test accuracy for a long time, and then abruptly generalises long after training loss has bottomed out. Named from Heinlein's coined verb 'to grok', meaning to understand something so thoroughly it becomes part of you.
definition_zh: 网络先把训练集背了下来，测试集准确率长期停留在随机水平，直到训练损失早已收敛之后很久，泛化能力才突然出现。名字来自海因莱因小说里生造的动词 grok——彻底理解到与之融为一体。
pitfalls: The most interesting entry in this category. Three problems compound. (1) 'Grok' is a Heinlein science-fiction coinage with no lexical history; nothing in Chinese carries that provenance, and every Chinese rendering silently drops it. (2) 顿悟 — the most common rendering — is a Chan/Zen Buddhist technical term (顿悟 'sudden awakening' vs 渐悟 'gradual awakening', the doctrinal split between the Southern and Northern schools). It imports a mystical register the English lacks, and worse it emphasises exactly the wrong half of the phenomenon: 顿悟 foregrounds suddenness, whereas the defining property of grokking is the long *delay*. A reader who only sees 顿悟 will not know that waiting is the point. (3) 顿悟 is now doubly booked: Chinese coverage of DeepSeek-R1 uses 顿悟时刻 for the RL 'aha moment', a completely different phenomenon. The cleanest solution, and what the better Chinese sources actually do, is to keep 'grokking' and gloss it functionally as 延迟泛化 (delayed generalization) — which loses the Heinlein joke but describes the thing correctly and collides with nothing.

alt_zh: 群体相对策略优化 / 群相对策略优化
definition_en: DeepSeek's critic-free RL algorithm: sample a group of responses to the same prompt, use their normalised relative rewards as the advantage, and drop the value network entirely. The workhorse of the DeepSeek-R1 era.
definition_zh: DeepSeek 提出的免价值网络强化学习算法：对同一个问题采样一组回答，用组内相对奖励做优势估计，从而完全去掉 critic。DeepSeek-R1 之后成为推理模型训练的主流算法。
pitfalls: The seed hypothesis that Chinese might be the primary language here does NOT hold. GRPO originated at DeepSeek but was published in English (DeepSeekMath, 2024) and named in English; Chinese sources treat 群体相对策略优化 as a translation of the English name, and it shows the instability of a translated term — 群体相对策略优化 competes with 群相对策略优化 and 组相对策略优化. A Chinese-origin technique can still have an English-origin name.

definition_en: Runtime filters and policies wrapped around a model — input classifiers, output classifiers, rule engines — that block disallowed content and behaviour without changing the model's weights.
definition_zh: 套在模型外面的运行时防护：输入分类器、输出分类器、规则引擎等，在不改动模型权重的前提下拦截不允许的内容和行为。
pitfalls: The metaphor transfers cleanly (护栏 is the ordinary word for a highway crash barrier), so there is no semantic problem. The register problem is that in China 安全护栏 has been claimed as a commercial product name — Alibaba Cloud ships 「AI 安全护栏（AI Guardrails）」 and Qwen3Guard is marketed as a 护栏模型 — so the term now reads as vendor vocabulary. In frontier-safety writing (where 'guardrails' is often used loosely for any safety measure) that commercial association can mislead. 防护栏 also appears but is less common.

definition_en: An agent that completes tasks by operating a graphical user interface — a phone or desktop screen — through perception of the UI plus simulated clicks and keystrokes.
definition_zh: 通过感知图形界面并模拟点击、输入来完成任务的智能体，覆盖手机端和桌面端。
pitfalls: Added because the Chinese term is more prominent and more stable than the English one, and because Chinese discourse centres the phone case (手机智能体) where English centres the desktop. Worth recording as an instance where the Chinese vocabulary is richer than the English.

definition_en: A model producing fluent, confident content that is simply not true — invented citations, biographies, prices, case law. A reliability failure rather than a safety failure in the frontier sense, but the one non-specialists know.
definition_zh: 模型生成流畅、自信但根本不存在的内容，比如编造的引文、人物生平、票价或判例。它属于可靠性问题而非前沿意义上的安全问题，但却是公众最熟悉的一种失效。
pitfalls: None. 幻觉 is universal and the metaphor transfers cleanly. Some Chinese writers note, as English ones do, that 虚构/编造 ('fabrication') would be more accurate than a perception metaphor, but this has not displaced 幻觉.

definition_en: The doctrinal framework, articulated by Xi Jinping in 2014, under which national security is defined to span a long enumerated list of domains — political, territorial, military, economic, cultural, social, S&T, cyber, ecological, resource, nuclear, biosecurity, and more, with AI, data, space, deep sea and polar security added in later formulations. It is the reason AI risk in PRC discourse is filed under national security rather than placed beside it.
definition_zh: 2014年提出的国家安全指导思想，把国家安全界定为涵盖政治、国土、军事、经济、文化、社会、科技、网络、生态、资源、核、生物等众多领域的整体，近年进一步纳入数据、人工智能、太空、深海、极地等新兴领域。它决定了人工智能安全在中国话语中被置于国家安全体系之内，而非与之并列。
pitfalls: 观 is an outlook or doctrinal worldview, not a 'concept' in the ordinary English sense — it belongs to the same grammatical family as 科学发展观 and marks canonical Party doctrine, which 'concept' badly understates. 总体 means 'taken as a whole / integral', not 'general'. The practical consequence for an English reader is the important one: because AI safety sits inside this frame, PRC documents treat content risk, ideological risk, supply-chain risk and technical loss-of-control risk as members of one category. Priorities that look arbitrary from outside — heavy attention to generated content, comparatively less to autonomous capability — are legible once this doctrine is in view.

alt_zh: 人机协作 / 人工审批 / 人类监督
definition_en: A design in which the system pauses before a consequential action and requires a human to review, approve, reject or edit it before continuing.
definition_zh: 一种设计模式：系统在做出关键判断或高风险动作前暂停，交由人审阅、批准、拒绝或修改后再继续。
pitfalls: Four renderings compete and they encode different amounts of control. 人在回路 is the most faithful (回路 = loop, from control theory) and is the emerging default in agent writing. 人机协作 / 人机协同 ('human-machine collaboration') is what MCP's Chinese documentation and much product copy use, and it is materially weaker — collaboration does not imply a blocking approval gate, so a Chinese spec that says 人机协作 may not actually require the human to be able to stop anything. 人工审批 ('manual approval') is the concrete engineering mechanism and is unambiguous but narrow. 人类监督 belongs to the regulatory register (EU AI Act Chinese translations) and covers supervision generally, not the in-loop pause. When translating a safety requirement, prefer 人在回路 or 人工审批 over 人机协作 — the last one quietly drops the veto.

alt_zh: 人工干预 / 人类控制
definition_en: The requirement that natural persons can effectively monitor, intervene in, override or shut down an AI system during its operation. A legal obligation under EU AI Act Article 14 and a recurring principle in PRC AI governance documents.
definition_zh: 要求在 AI 系统运行期间，自然人能够有效地监督它、介入它、推翻它的输出乃至停止它。这既是欧盟《人工智能法案》第 14 条的法定义务，也是中国 AI 治理文件中反复出现的原则。
pitfalls: Register split worth documenting. 人类监督 is the term used in Chinese translations of EU/international instruments (AI Act Art. 14). PRC-origin policy text reaches instead for 人工干预 (human intervention), 人类控制 (human control) and the compact formula 「确保人工智能始终处于人类控制之下」 (Global AI Governance Initiative, 2023) — note that 干预 is narrower than oversight (it names the act of stepping in, not the continuous watching), and 控制 is stronger. Separately, 监督 vs 监管: 监督 is oversight by a person in the loop; 监管 is regulatory supervision by an authority — do not swap them. Compare also the ML sense of 监督 in 监督学习 (supervised learning), a third unrelated meaning of the same characters.

definition_en: One of the security domains covered by the holistic national security concept, concerned with maintaining the dominant position of the state's guiding ideology and the integrity of the value system in public discourse. Its statutory anchor is Article 23 of the 2015 National Security Law, which provides that the state upholds the advancing direction of advanced socialist culture, cultivates and practises the core socialist values, guards against and resists the influence of undesirable culture, and holds the leading position in the ideological sphere. In AI regulation it functions as a named protected interest: TC260's AI Safety Governance Framework lists ideological security alongside citizens' lives and property, national security and ethical safety among the interests threatened by AI-generated content, and TC260-003 makes 'content violating the core socialist values' the first of the thirty-one risk types that generative services are tested against.
definition_zh: 总体国家安全观所涵盖的安全领域之一，指维护主流意识形态的主导地位与公共话语中价值体系的完整性。法条依据为《中华人民共和国国家安全法》第二十三条："国家坚持社会主义先进文化前进方向，继承和弘扬中华民族优秀传统文化，培育和践行社会主义核心价值观，防范和抵制不良文化的影响，掌握意识形态领域主导权，增强文化整体实力和竞争力。"在人工智能监管中，它是被点名的受保护法益：《人工智能安全治理框架》把"意识形态安全"与公民生命财产安全、国家安全、伦理安全并列为人工智能生成内容可能威胁的对象；TC260-003 将"包含违反社会主义核心价值观的内容"列为31种安全风险之首。
pitfalls: The English words are available and TC260's own English uses them, so the rendering is not in doubt; the risk is in reading. English 'ideology' is pejorative or at least contestable — an ideology is what other people have — whereas 意识形态 in this register is a neutral administrative category naming a domain of national security on the same footing as economic security or cybersecurity. Translating it accurately therefore requires resisting the temptation to editorialise in either direction. The analytical payoff is large: without this term, PRC AI content rules look like a grab-bag of arbitrary prohibitions; with it, they resolve into a coherent structure in which the capacity of a service to shape public discourse (舆论属性) is the jurisdictional trigger, ideological security is the protected interest, and 内容安全 is the operational control. Note also 意识形态 appears in PRC foreign-policy text in a different, critical sense — 'drawing ideological lines' (以意识形态划线) in the Global AI Governance Initiative — so the same characters carry a positive-domestic and a negative-international usage in documents issued weeks apart.

definition_en: A model's ability to pick up a task from examples placed in the prompt, without any weight update. The capability that made few-shot prompting work and that first marked LLMs as qualitatively different.
definition_zh: 模型仅凭提示中给出的少量示例就能学会一个任务，权重完全不更新。这是少样本提示之所以有效的原因，也是大模型区别于以往模型的标志性能力之一。
pitfalls: Mildly misleading on its own: 上下文学习 read literally suggests 'learning the context' rather than 'learning from what is in the context', and there is no 训练 in it at all despite 学习. Some Chinese writing adds 情境学习 or keeps ICL. The dominant form is nonetheless 上下文学习.

alt_zh: 事故报告机制 / 安全事件
definition_en: A duty or practice of recording and escalating AI failures, near-misses and misuse cases — to the developer's own risk process, to a regulator, or to an international mechanism.
definition_zh: 对人工智能故障、险情和滥用事件进行记录并向上报告的机制，报告对象可以是开发者内部的风险管理流程、监管部门，或国际层面的协调机制。
pitfalls: Three near-synonyms are in play and they are not interchangeable. 事件 is the neutral 'event/incident' and is what the technical AI-safety literature uses (事件报告). 事故 implies an accident with actual harm — IDAIS's Chinese text uses 事故报告机制, which reads more severe. 安全事件 is the established cybersecurity term and drags in the whole 应急响应 apparatus. Also note that PRC regulation attaches incident duties to 应急预案 (contingency plans) and 应急演练 (drills) rather than to a standalone reporting obligation, so 'incident reporting' as a discrete regulatory instrument is weaker in the PRC system than in the EU AI Act.

definition_en: An attention head (really a two-head composition) that implements the pattern [A][B] … [A] → [B]: it finds the earlier occurrence of the current token and copies whatever followed it. Widely argued to be the mechanistic basis of in-context learning.
definition_zh: 一种（实际由两层注意力头组合而成的）注意力头，实现 [A][B] … [A] → [B] 的规则：找到当前 token 上一次出现的位置，把当时的后继 token 复制过来。学界普遍认为它是上下文学习的机制基础。
pitfalls: A real false-friend risk in Chinese. English 'induction' here is logical induction — inferring a rule from repeated instances — which is 归纳 in Chinese. But 感应 also translates 'induction' (electromagnetic induction = 电磁感应), and 感应头 is attested in Chinese interpretability writing. Combined with the 电路 rendering of 'circuit', this pulls the whole vocabulary toward an electrical-engineering reading that the English does not have. 归纳头 is the semantically correct choice, but we could not recover a fetchable verbatim sentence using it, and the safest observed practice is simply to keep the English: 集智's reading-group agenda literally writes 'Hello World回路：induction head'. Note also that a Chinese reader may parse 头 as 'head' in the anatomical sense; 注意力头 (attention head) is however fully established, so the compound is understandable.

definition_en: Whether the objective a model actually optimizes internally matches the training objective it was given. Inner alignment failures are invisible in the loss and show up as goal misgeneralization or deceptive alignment.
definition_zh: 指模型内部真正优化的目标，是否与人类赋予它的训练目标一致。内部对齐失败在损失函数上看不出来，通常表现为目标错误泛化或欺骗性对齐。
pitfalls: The inner/outer distinction survives translation cleanly as 内部/外部对齐, and the Chinese survey literature treats the pair as settled consensus. One wrinkle: Chinese Wikipedia frames the pair negatively, as 内部未对齐 / 外部未对齐 (inner/outer *mis*alignment), so both polarities circulate. Also note 内部对齐 can be misread by a lay reader as 'internal coordination' within an organisation.

definition_en: A 2025 training-time intervention: prepend a system prompt that explicitly instructs the model to exhibit the undesired behaviour (reward hacking, sycophancy, a narrow misaligned trait) during fine-tuning. Because the behaviour is already explained by the instruction, gradient pressure to internalise it drops, and the test-time model expresses it far less.
definition_zh: 2025 年提出的训练期干预手段：在微调数据的系统提示里明确要求模型表现出那个不想要的行为（比如奖励作弊、谄媚）。既然该行为已由指令解释，模型就不必把它内化成自身倾向，测试时反而表现得更少。
pitfalls: GENUINE GAP. Repeated Chinese-language searches (接种提示 / 免疫提示 / 疫苗提示 combined with 大模型, 对齐, 奖励黑客) returned no Chinese-language treatment of this technique at all — every result was the English arXiv/LessWrong/Anthropic material or an unrelated prompt-injection page. As of this research date the term appears to have no Chinese presence whatsoever. Beyond absence, the metaphor is the hard part: English 'inoculation' carries a vaccine frame (a controlled dose of the bad thing confers resistance). 免疫提示 names the effect (immunity) but not the mechanism; 接种式提示 names the mechanism (inoculating/vaccinating) and is the closer calque — 接种 is the standard Chinese verb for administering a vaccine, so the medical metaphor transfers cleanly. 疫苗提示 (vaccine prompt) is punchier but reads as marketing. Note also the potential collision with 提示注入 (prompt injection), which is superficially similar in shape (both insert an instruction) but adversarial rather than defensive.

alt_zh: 内部人员威胁 / 内鬼 / 强化内部安全管理
definition_en: Risk originating from someone with legitimate access — an employee, contractor or partner — who exfiltrates weights, disables safeguards or subverts controls.
definition_zh: 由拥有合法访问权限的人员（员工、承包商、合作方）带来的风险，例如外泄模型权重、关闭防护措施或规避管控。
pitfalls: 内部威胁 is the standard security-industry calque, but in the leading Chinese frontier-AI risk framework the same two characters mean something entirely different: there, 威胁源 is split into 外部威胁 (malicious actors, terrorists), 内部威胁 — glossed explicitly as 模型自身的未对齐或欺骗倾向, i.e. the model itself — and 情境性威胁 (human operator error). So in Chinese AI-safety writing 内部威胁 can denote *the AI* rather than a rogue human. This is a real and easily-missed false friend. If you mean a malicious employee, disambiguate: 内部人员威胁 or 内部人员风险. The colloquial 内鬼 ('inside ghost', a mole) is vivid and widely understood but too informal for policy prose, and no attestation for it was recovered in an AI context.

alt_zh: 工具趋同 / 工具趋同目标
definition_en: The claim that agents with very different final goals will nonetheless converge on the same intermediate goals — self-preservation, self-improvement, resource acquisition — because those subgoals help achieve almost any final goal.
definition_zh: 该论点认为，最终目标差别很大的智能体，往往会趋同到同一批中间目标上，例如自我保持、自我增强和资源获取，因为这些子目标几乎有助于实现任何最终目标。
pitfalls: The rendering is stable in academic Chinese but fragments in the wild: 工具性趋同 / 工具趋同 / 工具性目标趋同 / 工具趋同目标 all appear, and Chinese Wikipedia treats 工具趋同目标 as a synonym for 'power-seeking' rather than as a separate thesis. 趋同 (converge, as in biology) is a good choice; 收敛 would import an optimisation-theory reading and should be avoided. Note that 工具性 alone can be misread as 'utilitarian' or 'merely a tool', losing the means-to-an-end sense.

definition_en: I. J. Good's 1965 hypothesis that a machine capable of improving machine design would produce a rapid, self-reinforcing cascade of capability gains, leaving human intelligence far behind.
definition_zh: 古德 1965 年提出的假说：一台能够改进机器设计的机器将引发能力上的自我强化式快速级联增长，最终把人类智能远远抛在身后。
pitfalls: The calque is transparent and does carry Good's lineage in Chinese popular-science writing, which retells the 1965 argument accurately. The register is the issue: 智能爆炸 appears in think-pieces, 集智俱乐部 explainers and business media, but is absent from both authoritative documents checked here — zero occurrences in the 189-page Chinese 2026 International AI Safety Report and none in the TC260 framework. It also travels in the company of 奇点 (singularity), which drags Kurzweil-flavoured futurism along with it; a Chinese reader may hear the phrase as sci-fi rather than as a forecasting hypothesis. Variant 智能大爆炸 borrows the phrasing of 宇宙大爆炸 (the Big Bang) and reads more dramatic still.

definition_en: A datacentre built specifically to serve AI training and inference — accelerator-dense, often described by its FLOPS rating and by whether it hosts 万卡级 (10,000-accelerator-class) clusters — as distinct from a general-purpose 数据中心 and from a 超算中心 (HPC/supercomputing centre). Contraction of 智能计算中心.
definition_zh: 面向人工智能训练与推理建设的算力设施，以智能算力（加速卡）为主，常以 PFLOPS 规模和是否部署万卡级集群来描述，区别于通用数据中心和超算中心。是“智能计算中心”的缩略。
pitfalls: 'Intelligent computing centre' is the standard rendering and is close to meaningless in English — it sounds like a smart-building or a service desk, not a GPU datacentre. The real risks in reading PRC compute reporting are categorical: 智算中心 (AI datacentre), 超算中心 (supercomputing centre) and 数据中心 (general datacentre) are three tracked, separately-planned categories, and English coverage flattens all three to 'data centre', which makes provincial buildout figures incomparable. Note also that 智算 is a contraction of 智能计算 and appears in 智算集群 / 智算枢纽 / 智算资源, none of which have settled English forms — CSET's translation of the State Council 'AI Plus' Opinions uses 'intelligent computing cluster' and 'intelligent compute infrastructure' for the neighbouring terms. Finally, headline PFLOPS figures for 智算中心 are usually quoted at low precision (FP16/INT8) and are not comparable with FP64 supercomputer ratings.

preferred_zh: 《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》
definition_en: China's operative generative-AI regulation, adopted by the CAC with six other ministries and in force from 15 August 2023. It establishes security assessment, algorithm filing and complaint mechanisms, allocates provider responsibilities, and applies to services offered to the public in mainland China.
definition_zh: 中国生成式人工智能的主要规章，由国家互联网信息办公室会同六部门公布，自 2023 年 8 月 15 日起施行。规定了安全评估、算法备案、投诉举报等制度，明确提供者责任，适用于向境内公众提供生成式人工智能服务的行为。
pitfalls: Chinese-origin instrument — cite the Chinese text. Every word of the title does work: 暂行 (interim/provisional) signals that a fuller instrument is expected; 办法 is a departmental rule (部门规章), which sits below a 法律 (law) and 行政法规 (administrative regulation) in the PRC hierarchy — so 'Measures' is right and 'Act' or 'Law' would be wrong; 管理 is administration, deliberately softer than 监管. And 服务 matters: the Measures regulate *services offered to the public*, not model development as such, which is why research and internal use fall outside them. Note that the substantive obligations run through cross-references to other instruments (the algorithm-recommendation provisions, the security-assessment regime), so the Measures read thinner than they operate.

alt_zh: 国际人工智能治理 / 全球公共产品
definition_en: Cross-border coordination on AI rules, standards and risk management — through the UN, summit processes, standards bodies and bilateral channels.
definition_zh: 各国就人工智能规则、标准和风险管理开展的跨境协调，载体包括联合国机制、峰会进程、标准化组织和双边渠道。
pitfalls: 全球 and 国际 are both available and PRC official discourse strongly prefers 全球人工智能治理 — 《全球人工智能治理倡议》, 《全球人工智能治理行动计划》, 全球人工智能治理体系. 国际 tends to attach to bodies and processes (国际人工智能治理机构, 国际交流合作) rather than to the field as a whole. The choice is not stylistic: 全球 carries the inclusive, developing-country-facing framing the PRC advances, while 国际 reads as inter-state. Separately, 治理 (governance) is deliberately broader than 监管 (regulation) and is preferred in international texts precisely because it does not imply a supranational regulator.

alt_zh: 《高等人工智能安全国际科学报告》
definition_en: The scientific synthesis on general-purpose AI risks chaired by Yoshua Bengio, first published 29 January 2025 with contributions nominated by 30 countries plus the EU, OECD and UN. Chinese experts including Zeng Yi sit on its expert advisory panel; Andrew Yao and Zhang Ya-Qin are senior advisers.
definition_zh: 由图灵奖得主 Yoshua Bengio 担任主席的通用人工智能风险科学综述报告，首份报告于 2025 年 1 月 29 日发布，由 30 个国家及欧盟、经合组织、联合国提名的专家参与。中国科学院自动化研究所曾毅等中国学者参加专家顾问组，姚期智、张亚勤担任高级顾问。
pitfalls: Two names circulate because the report itself was renamed: the interim version was the 'International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI', rendered 《高等人工智能安全国际科学报告》, before it became the International AI Safety Report / 《国际人工智能安全报告》. Chinese sources sometimes give both. Note that the report's Chinese title uses 安全, so a reader cannot tell from the title alone that its subject is safety rather than security — the content settles it.

preferred_zh: 人工智能安全国际对话
alt_zh: 北京AI安全国际对话 / 《人工智能红线共识声明》
definition_en: A track-two dialogue series convening senior AI scientists from China and the West, organised by the Safe AI Forum. Meetings: Oxford (2023), Beijing (March 2024), Venice (September 2024), Shanghai (July 2025), London (April 2026). Each issues a consensus statement in parallel English and Chinese.
definition_zh: 由 Safe AI Forum 组织的二轨对话系列，汇集中西方资深人工智能科学家，已举办牛津（2023）、北京（2024 年 3 月）、威尼斯（2024 年 9 月）、上海（2025 年 7 月）、伦敦（2026 年 4 月）等届，每届发布中英文对照的共识声明。
pitfalls: The name is not stable in Chinese. Safe AI Forum's own Chinese page uses 人工智能安全国际对话（IDAIS）; Tsinghua AIR and Chinese media covering the Beijing meeting used 北京AI安全国际对话; and 国际人工智能安全对话 also circulates. Word order matters: 人工智能安全国际对话 = 'international dialogue on AI safety' (the English), whereas 国际人工智能安全对话 parses as 'dialogue on international AI safety'. Prefer the first. The Beijing statement's own Chinese title is 《北京AI安全国际共识》 / 《人工智能红线共识声明》, not a translation of 'IDAIS'. The bilingual statements are the single highest-value attestation source in this category — quote them directly.

definition_en: The general project of making a model's internal computation or its outputs intelligible to humans. In AI safety it is load-bearing: you cannot verify that a model is not deceiving you if you cannot inspect what it is doing.
definition_zh: 让人类能够理解模型的内部计算过程或其输出依据的研究方向。在 AI 安全语境下，它是验证模型是否"表里如一"的前提——看不懂模型在做什么，就无法确认它没有欺骗你。
pitfalls: 可解释性 is fully established but is doing double duty. In the older Chinese XAI/ML-security literature (2019-2022) it means post-hoc explanation of a prediction — saliency maps, LIME/SHAP, feature attribution. In the newer Anthropic-lineage literature it means reverse-engineering the computation itself. Chinese writers do not have separate words for these, so a claim that a system 具有可解释性 can mean anything from 'we plotted a heatmap' to 'we traced the circuit'. In the PRC policy register 可解释性 additionally sits next to 透明性 and is treated as a compliance property, not a research programme. 可理解性 exists but is rare; 可释性 is not used.

definition_en: A model's ability to accurately report on its own internal states. Anthropic's 2025 concept-injection experiments found Claude Opus 4/4.1 could detect an injected concept in roughly 20% of trials — limited and unreliable, but above chance.
definition_zh: 模型能否准确报告自己的内部状态。Anthropic 2025 年的概念注入实验发现 Claude Opus 4/4.1 大约在 20% 的试验里能察觉被注入的概念——能力有限也不稳定，但高于随机。
pitfalls: 内省 is the established philosophy/psychology term and transfers cleanly. The one thing to watch is that Chinese popular coverage slides between 内省 (introspection, reporting internal states) and 自我反思 / 反思 (self-reflection, reconsidering a conclusion) — these are different claims, and the 澎湃 coverage explicitly flags the distinction. Also note 自省 exists and means 'self-examination' with a moral flavour (as in 吾日三省吾身); avoid it for the technical sense. Guard against the term implying consciousness claims that the research does not make.

definition_en: A contraction of 信息技术应用创新, naming the programme and the industry built around replacing foreign components of the IT stack — CPUs, operating systems, databases, middleware, office software — with domestic equivalents, and the certified-compatible product ecosystem that results. It is the operational, procurement-level expression of the self-reliance goals stated at policy level as 自主可控 and 科技自立自强.
definition_zh: “信息技术应用创新”的缩略语，指以国产芯片、操作系统、数据库、中间件、办公软件等替代国外产品的产业与工程，以及围绕适配认证形成的产品生态。它是政策层面“自主可控”“科技自立自强”在采购和落地层面的具体形态。
pitfalls: The name is actively unhelpful. 'IT application innovation' says nothing about substitution, which is the entire content of the concept — a reader who meets the English rendering cold will assume it means innovation in applying IT. The obscurity appears to be a feature of the term's origin rather than an accident of translation. Note also the register finding below: this is a procurement, vendor and equity-research word, not a central policy word, so its absence from a State Council document is not evidence that the policy is absent — it will be expressed there as 自主可控.

definition_en: Paul Christiano's scalable-oversight scheme: decompose a hard task into easier subtasks that a human plus copies of a weaker model can handle (amplification), then distil the amplified overseer back into a single model, and iterate.
definition_zh: Christiano 提出的可扩展监督方案：把难任务分解成人类和若干弱模型副本能处理的子任务（放大），再把放大后的监督者蒸馏回单个模型，如此反复迭代。
pitfalls: Two problems. (1) The abbreviation IDA is unusable in Chinese search space: 「IDA」 overwhelmingly returns IDA* (迭代加深A*搜索), a classical search algorithm, and IDA Pro the disassembler. (2) Chinese sources overwhelmingly render only the short form 迭代放大; the full 迭代蒸馏与放大 is essentially unattested, and 蒸馏 in Chinese ML now strongly means knowledge distillation between models (and, since 2025, model-theft policy discourse), so restoring it would mislead more than help.

definition_en: An input, or family of inputs, that gets a model to do something its safety training was meant to prevent — typically by reframing, roleplay, obfuscation or encoding the request.
definition_zh: 通过改写、角色扮演、混淆或编码等手段构造输入，使模型突破安全训练所设的限制，输出本应被拒绝的内容。
pitfalls: None serious. 越狱 arrives via the iOS-jailbreaking sense and is fully naturalised; the metaphor (breaking out of prison) survives translation intact. In agent-security writing 提示词越狱 ('prompt jailbreak') is used for the single-turn case, in contrast with multi-step agent attacks.

alt_zh: KYC / 真实身份信息认证
definition_en: Verifying who a customer is before granting service. In AI governance it is proposed for cloud compute providers, so that large training runs cannot be bought anonymously.
definition_zh: 在提供服务前核实客户身份的制度。在人工智能治理中，主要提议用于云算力服务商，使大规模训练无法匿名购买。
pitfalls: Three separate problems. (1) Chinese practitioners usually just write KYC in Latin letters; 了解你的客户 / 认识你的客户 are glosses, and 认识你的客戶 is the Taiwan/HK form. (2) I could not verify any Chinese-language source applying KYC to AI compute providers, so the AI-governance sense appears not to have entered Chinese discourse at all — a genuine gap. (3) 实名制 / 真实身份信息认证 is a real and heavily enforced PRC regime that partly overlaps KYC but is not the same thing: it verifies the *end user* of an internet service against a national ID or mobile number, it exists for content-attribution and public-security reasons rather than anti-money-laundering, and it has never been applied to compute purchasing. Do not use 实名制 to translate KYC in a compute-governance argument; explain the difference instead.

definition_en: A neural language model with a very large parameter count trained on massive text corpora, used for language tasks such as generation, translation and summarisation.
definition_zh: 指参数规模极大、在海量文本语料上训练的神经网络语言模型，用于文本生成、翻译、摘要等语言任务。
pitfalls: Unproblematic, with one caveat for the ZH→EN direction: Chinese writers very often drop to the bare 大模型, which is broader than 'LLM' (it also covers multimodal and non-language models). Rendering every 大模型 as 'LLM' over-specifies. 大型语言模型 and 大语言模型 are freely interchangeable; official translations tend to 大型语言模型, industry to 大语言模型.

definition_en: The default Chinese umbrella noun for the post-2022 foundation-model paradigm: any large-scale pretrained model that is adapted to many downstream tasks. It covers LLMs, multimodal and vision-language models, and industry-specific fine-tunes, and is used as a paradigm label rather than a parameter-count threshold — a 4B fine-tune shipped as a product is still 大模型.
definition_zh: 指经大规模数据预训练、可适配多种下游任务的基础模型，是 2022 年以来中文语境中对这一技术范式最通用的称呼。既涵盖通用基础模型，也涵盖垂直行业模型；在中文里它更接近“基础模型/大模型范式”，而不是一个参数量门槛。
pitfalls: 'Large model' is a calque, not idiomatic English — no English-speaking practitioner says it unprompted, yet it is the rendering used in TC260's own official English text and in most translated PRC material, so an English reader meets it constantly. Two specific traps: (1) 大模型 is a paradigm claim, not a size claim, so '大模型' routinely covers models an English writer would call small (Qwen3-4B, industry fine-tunes) — reading it as 'large' imports a false size threshold; (2) it is broader than 'LLM' (it includes multimodal, vision-language-action and diffusion-family models when they are pretrained-and-adapted) but narrower than 'AI model' (a bespoke task-specific classifier is not 大模型). 'Foundation model' is the accurate English concept and 上海AI实验室/安远AI explicitly equate the two, but it is not what translations say. Also note the productive compounds — 大模型备案, 大模型安全, 通用大模型 vs 行业大模型 — which have no single-word English counterparts.

definition_en: A regime in which an activity is prohibited unless a regulator has granted permission in advance. Proposed for frontier AI training and deployment; not the instrument China actually uses for AI.
definition_zh: 未经监管部门事先批准即不得从事某项活动的制度。国际上有人主张对前沿人工智能的训练和部署实行许可制，但中国目前对人工智能采用的并非许可制。
pitfalls: The essential point in this category. Chinese administrative law distinguishes 行政许可 (administrative licensing — prohibited unless permitted, governed by the 行政许可法) from 备案 (filing — permitted, but you must record it). China's AI regime is built on 备案, not 许可. English writing that calls China's algorithm/model filing a 'licensing regime' overstates the state's gatekeeping power; conversely, Chinese writing that renders proposals for frontier-AI 'licensing' as 备案 understates them. Keep the pair distinct: 许可 = licence/permission, 备案 = filing. 牌照 is the informal industry word for a licence-as-asset (telecom, finance) and carries a market-access connotation; 审批 (approval) is a third adjacent term. CAICT's report is explicit that traditional 物理准入许可 tools are failing for AI.

definition_en: Applying the model's output head (unembedding) to hidden states at intermediate layers, so that each layer's residual stream can be read as a distribution over the vocabulary — showing how the model's guess evolves layer by layer.
definition_zh: 把模型最后的输出头（解嵌入矩阵）直接作用在中间层的隐藏状态上，于是每一层的残差流都能被读成一个词表上的概率分布，从而看到模型的"猜测"是如何逐层演变的。
pitfalls: Effectively untranslated. The head noun 'lens' would go to 透镜, but the modifier cannot be rendered: 'logit' has no Chinese equivalent in ML usage at all — Chinese papers and blogs write logit / logits in Latin letters inside Chinese sentences, exactly as they do for token and embedding. So any Chinese rendering ends up as a hybrid (logit 透镜), which is why writers mostly keep the whole phrase. Chinese explanations of the method are written descriptively ("把中间层的隐藏状态投影到词表空间") rather than with a term. Note also that Chinese sources frequently write 'Logits Lens' with an s, which the English literature does not. Do not treat 'tuned lens' as a synonym: it is a later, distinct method (Belrose et al. 2023) that trains a separate affine probe per layer precisely because applying the unembedding directly is brittle; Chinese writing keeps it in English too.

alt_zh: 长期任务 / 长程自主性 / 长时程任务
definition_en: A task requiring many interdependent steps sustained over a long period. METR measures capability as the human-equivalent task length a model can complete at a 50% success rate.
definition_zh: 需要连续完成大量相互依赖步骤、跨越较长时间的任务。METR 用「模型在 50% 成功率下能完成的任务对应的人类耗时」来衡量这项能力。
pitfalls: Three renderings are live and none has fully won: 长程任务 (favoured in 2026 academic survey writing, and the basis of 长程智能体 for 'long-horizon agent'), 长时程任务 (more literal, spells out the time dimension), and 长期任务 (used by tech media but ambiguous — it can just mean 'an ongoing/standing task' in ordinary Chinese). Separately, METR's 'time horizon' metric is rendered 时间跨度, which is a different word from any of the above, so a reader following the Chinese coverage sees 长期任务 and 时间跨度 in the same article without an obvious link. Safety-register writing (安远 AI) uses a fourth form, 长程自主性, for 'long-horizon autonomy' as a capability category.

alt_zh: 失去控制 / 控制权丧失
definition_en: A scenario in which one or more AI systems operate outside any human's control and there is no clear route to regaining it. Distinct from an ordinary malfunction: the system continues to act competently, just not under human direction.
definition_zh: 指AI系统的运行脱离所有人的控制，且没有明确途径重新夺回控制权的情形。它与普通故障不同——系统仍在有效地行动，只是不再听命于人。
pitfalls: 失控 is the near-universal rendering and is now locked in by both the Chinese translation of the International AI Safety Report and by PRC policy text, so it must be used. But it is a broad, colloquial word — Chinese uses 失控 for cars, emotions, crowds, epidemics and budgets — and it carries none of the technical content of the English term (no implication of a capable agent, no 'no path to regain control' clause). Note the register split: in PRC governance text 失控 usually means the *state or regulator* losing control over a technology, whereas in the alignment literature it means *humanity* losing control over an agent. Serious sources therefore gloss it on first use rather than let it stand alone; the IAISR Chinese translation does exactly this. 控制权丧失 and 丧失控制 are more precise but are not idiomatic and did not appear as fixed terms in any source located.

definition_en: One of the three top-level risk categories of the International AI Safety Report — risks where AI systems fail or behave in unexpected and harmful ways — comprising reliability failures and loss of control. 故障风险 is the Chinese edition's rendering of 'risks from malfunctions'; it is a translated taxonomy term, not a term of PRC origin.
definition_zh: 《国际人工智能安全报告》三大风险类别之一，指人工智能系统出现故障或以意料之外的有害方式运行的风险，下辖“可靠性挑战”与“失控”两节。该词是英文 risks from malfunctions 的中译，并非中国本土分类术语。
pitfalls: The framing to be careful about is real but its provenance is the opposite of what is usually assumed. Filing loss of control under a 'malfunction' heading originates in the International AI Safety Report (chaired by Yoshua Bengio) — §2.2 Risks from malfunctions contains §2.2.1 Reliability challenges and §2.2.2 Loss of control — and 故障风险 is simply the Chinese edition's translation of that heading.
