It is NOT the PRC taxonomy category for loss of control. The two authoritative PRC taxonomies file 失控 elsewhere: TC260's national AI Safety Governance Framework puts '“自我意识”觉醒、脱离人类控制' under 3.3.2 伦理安全风险 (ethical safety risks), inside the 应用衍生安全风险 (derivative) tier — i.e. as an ethics-and-society risk, not an engineering fault; and the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia AI Frontier AI Risk Management Framework promotes 失控风险 to a top-level domain of its own, defined by threat source '模型破坏控制的倾向', while routing genuine engineering faults into a separate 意外风险 (accident) domain. So the structural divergence between the Chinese and English literatures runs the other way: the PRC documents *decline* the malfunction framing that the international report adopts. Separately, in ordinary PRC engineering prose 故障风险 just means 'failure risk' (e.g. 级联故障, 单点故障) with no taxonomic force.

alt_zh: 机械可解释性 / mechanistic interpretability
definition_en: Reverse-engineering the algorithms a neural network actually implements — identifying features, the circuits that connect them, and the causal role each plays — rather than explaining individual predictions after the fact.
definition_zh: 把神经网络当作一段需要逆向工程的程序来研究：找出模型内部的特征、特征之间构成的回路，以及每一部分在计算中承担的因果作用，而不是事后为某个预测编一个解释。
pitfalls: Genuinely contested between 机制可解释性 and 机械可解释性, and the difference matters. 机制 = mechanism (as in 作用机制, 'mechanism of action', the sense Chris Olah intends). 机械 = mechanical / machine-like, and in ordinary Chinese 机械 carries a strong pejorative sense of 'rigid, rote, unthinking' (机械地照搬 = to copy mechanically). 机械可解释性 is a plausible-looking mistranslation that is nevertheless in real use, including in translated paper abstracts — the hint that it is 'a plausible mistranslation worth flagging' is confirmed, but it is not rare. Recommend 机制可解释性. A third common move is to keep the English inline: 机器之心 writes 'mechanistic interpretability（机制可解释性）'.

definition_en: When the model produced by a training process is itself an optimizer, searching over options according to its own objective. The training algorithm is the base optimizer; the learned optimizer inside the model is the mesa-optimizer, and its objective need not match the base objective.
definition_zh: 指训练过程产出的模型本身也是一个优化器，会按照自己的目标函数在可能的空间中搜索。训练算法称为基优化器，模型内部学到的优化器称为内优化器，二者的目标未必一致。
pitfalls: The Greek prefix is dropped, not transliterated: Chinese uses the 内/基 (inner/base) opposition, which is arguably clearer than the English 'mesa/base' but loses the deliberate coinage and breaks the link to the source literature. Because 内 is doing the work, Chinese texts almost always gloss with the English 'Mesa-optimizer' in parentheses on first use, and practitioners frequently just write 'mesa 优化器' in mixed script. There is no settled noun for the *process* 'mesa-optimization' — Chinese names the object (内优化器) and describes the process.

definition_en: Harm caused by people deliberately using an AI system to do something damaging — cyberattacks, bioweapon uplift, fraud, manipulation, non-consensual imagery. The system works as designed; the user's intent is the problem.
definition_zh: 指人有意利用AI系统去做有害的事：网络攻击、协助制造生物武器、诈骗、操纵、生成非自愿影像等。系统本身按设计运转，问题出在使用者的意图。
pitfalls: Easy to translate, and worth noting *why*: this is the risk category PRC discourse is most comfortable with, because it locates the danger in a human bad actor rather than in the technology or in anyone's governance. The asymmetry is visible in how much more developed the Chinese vocabulary is here (滥用, 恶意使用, 恶意利用, 违法使用) than for loss-of-control concepts. Distinguish the two main options: 恶意使用 specifies malicious intent and is the choice of the Chinese translation of the International AI Safety Report; 滥用 is broader and covers careless or excessive use as well as malicious use, so it is not a precise equivalent of 'malicious use'.

definition_en: An architecture in which a router activates only a few of many feed-forward "expert" sub-networks per token, so total parameters can be large while per-token compute stays small.
definition_zh: 模型里有很多个前馈「专家」子网络，路由器为每个 token 只激活其中少数几个，因此总参数量可以很大而单 token 计算量很小。DeepSeek、Qwen 的大模型普遍采用这种架构。
pitfalls: Chinese labs writing in Chinese overwhelmingly write MoE rather than 混合专家 — Qwen's own Chinese release blog says MoE 模型 throughout. 混合专家模型 is correct and understood, but is the gloss, not the working term. Note 总参数 / 激活参数 (total vs activated parameters) as the standard Chinese pair for describing MoE size.

definition_en: A published document accompanying a model release that states its intended use, training data, evaluation results, limitations and safety properties. A system card covers the deployed system rather than the bare model and is where frontier labs now publish their safety test results.
definition_zh: 随模型发布的公开文档，说明模型的用途、训练数据、评测结果、局限性与安全特性。系统卡描述的是部署后的整体系统而非单个模型，目前是前沿实验室公布安全测试结果的主要载体。
pitfalls: Minor. 模型卡 / 系统卡 are settled; the fuller 模型卡片 / 系统卡片 also occurs. Chinese frontier-safety writing consistently pairs them as 模型卡/系统卡 rather than choosing one. Note a substantive rather than linguistic caveat: Chinese labs' 技术报告 and 模型卡 generally do not include the dangerous-capability evaluation sections that the term implies in a frontier-safety context, so a Chinese reader may not associate 模型卡 with safety disclosure at all.

definition_en: An open protocol standardising how applications supply context, tools and resources to LLMs, so any client can talk to any tool server without bespoke integration.
definition_zh: 一种开放协议，统一了应用向大模型提供上下文、工具和资源的方式，使任意客户端都能对接任意工具服务端，无需为每个组合单独开发。
pitfalls: The Chinese name is settled and uncontested, but the abbreviation MCP is what people actually say and write — Chinese docs typically give 模型上下文协议（Model Context Protocol，简称 MCP）once and then use MCP throughout. Minor variant 大模型上下文协议 appears in some media headlines. One thing worth flagging for safety readers: MCP's Chinese docs render the sampling feature's human-approval design as 人机协作（Human-in-the-loop）rather than 人在回路, so the protocol's oversight vocabulary does not line up with the HITL vocabulary used elsewhere in Chinese agent-safety writing.

definition_en: Deliberately constructed misaligned models, built so that a failure mode that is otherwise only argued about philosophically can be studied empirically. The framing is borrowed from biology's use of C. elegans, Drosophila and mice. Hubinger et al., 2023.
definition_zh: 刻意造出来的失准模型，目的是把原本只能靠哲学论证讨论的失败模式变成可以做实验的对象。这个说法借自生物学里用线虫、果蝇、小鼠做研究的传统。出自 Hubinger 等人 2023 年的提法。
pitfalls: NO CHINESE AI-SAFETY USAGE FOUND. 模式生物 is the completely standard Chinese term for biology's model organisms and is well understood, so the metaphor is available in principle. But no Chinese-language AI-safety source using it for misaligned models was located in this pass, and Chinese coverage of the underlying papers (sleeper agents, reward tampering, alignment faking) describes the experiments without ever naming the methodology. Two further hazards: 模型生物 is a wrong-but-tempting variant (it back-translates as 'model creature' and is not the biology term), and in an AI context 模型 immediately means 'the ML model', so 模型生物 will be misparsed. If you must render it, use 失准模式生物 or 对齐失败的模式生物 and gloss the biology metaphor explicitly — Chinese readers will not infer it.

alt_zh: 大模型备案 / 登记备案 / 注册
definition_en: A requirement that a model or algorithmic service be recorded with a regulator before or shortly after it goes to market. China operates the world's only large-scale live regime of this kind: 算法备案 under the 2022 algorithm-recommendation rules, extended to generative AI in 2023.
definition_zh: 要求模型或算法服务在上线前后向监管部门登记的制度。中国是目前唯一大规模实际运行此类制度的国家：依《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》开展算法备案，2023 年经《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》扩展至生成式人工智能服务（大模型备案）。
pitfalls: This is the single most important asymmetry in the category. 备案 is a *filing* — the provider submits materials and the regulator records them; it is not an approval and is legally weaker than 许可 (licensing). English coverage that renders 备案 as 'licensing' or 'approval' materially overstates it. Chinese practice further distinguishes 算法备案 (the algorithm/service, filed with CAC's national system), 大模型备案 (the generative model, handled through provincial CAC offices) and 登记 (registration of downstream apps that merely call an already-filed model). Meanwhile the IDAIS statements use 注册 for the arms-control-style 'registration of training runs above a threshold' — a third word for a third concept. Pick deliberately: 备案 = the existing PRC filing regime; 注册 = a proposed international registry; 登记 = a lighter recording step.

alt_zh: 模型行为规范 / Model Spec
definition_en: OpenAI's published document specifying how its models should behave — objectives, hard rules, and default behaviours — used as the reference for training and for adjudicating disputed model responses.
definition_zh: OpenAI 公开发布的、规定其模型应当如何行为的文档，分为目标、规则和默认行为三层，既作为训练（尤其是 RLHF 标注）的依据，也作为判定模型回复是否恰当的参照。
pitfalls: 模型规范 is the settled rendering but is weaker than the English: 规范 in Chinese engineering usage means a technical specification or norm (like a coding 规范), which undersells that the document is a normative statement of intended values and behaviour, closer to a code of conduct. 行为规范 (code of conduct) is more accurate to the content and does appear in Chinese coverage. Also note the collision risk with 模型备案/技术规范 in PRC regulatory vocabulary, where 规范 means a formal standards document with legal weight — a Chinese policy reader may over-read the term's authority. No Chinese lab has published a direct equivalent document under this name at the time of research; Chinese labs express intended behaviour through 模型卡, 安全策略 and 使用规范 instead.

alt_zh: 模型权重 / 模型权重采用极端隔离存储策略
definition_en: Protecting the trained parameters of a frontier model from theft or unauthorised copying, since possession of the weights confers the model's full capability without any of its deployment safeguards. RAND's SL1–SL5 scale is the reference security-level framework.
definition_zh: 防止前沿模型的训练参数被窃取或未经授权复制。一旦获得权重，攻击者即可绕过所有部署侧防护措施，完整获得模型能力。兰德公司提出的 SL1–SL5 安全等级是常见参照框架。
pitfalls: 模型权重 is fully settled, so the compound is transparent — but 安全 again collapses safety and security, and here the intended sense is unambiguously *security*. Consider 模型权重防护 or 模型权重安全防护 when the distinction matters. The bigger issue is that Chinese frontier-AI practice reaches for a different reference framework: rather than RAND's SL1–SL5, Chinese guidance maps weight protection onto 网络安全等级保护 (MLPS), requiring at least 三级（监督保护级）for models past a risk threshold. The two scales are not comparable and should never be equated — MLPS grades a whole information system's protection obligations under PRC law, while SL1–SL5 grades resistance to specified attacker capability tiers.

definition_en: The target property of an interpretability decomposition: each recovered unit corresponds to exactly one human-legible concept. The goal SAEs pursue, and the title concept of Anthropic's 2023 Towards Monosemanticity.
definition_zh: 可解释性分解所追求的性质：分解出来的每个单元只对应一个人类能理解的概念。它是训练 SAE 的目标，也是 Anthropic 2023 年 Towards Monosemanticity 一文的核心概念。
pitfalls: Added because it is the antonym that makes 多义性 usable, and it inherits the same unresolved split: 单义性 (matching 多义性) vs 单语义性 (matching 多语义性). Chinese renderings of Anthropic's paper title used 单语义性; Chinese renderings of SAE surveys use 单义. Pick one and stay consistent with whichever you chose for polysemanticity. Also note 单义 is sometimes written adjectivally as 单义的特征 rather than as an abstract noun.

definition_en: A halt on developing or deploying systems above some capability level, whether self-imposed by a developer, agreed across an industry, or mandated. The FLI open letter of March 2023 calling for a six-month pause is the canonical instance.
definition_zh: 对超过一定能力水平的系统停止开发或部署，可以是开发者自我约束、行业共同约定或由监管强制。最有代表性的是 2023 年 3 月生命未来研究所发起的呼吁暂停六个月的公开信。
pitfalls: 暂停 (suspend, temporarily) is the natural and attested word, but it is weaker than English 'moratorium', which implies a formal, agreed, bounded halt. 禁令 (ban/injunction) is far stronger and implies legal prohibition — do not use it for a voluntary pause. 停止 is permanent-sounding. The Chinese-language conversation around the 2023 pause letter was largely framed as 呼吁暂停训练 rather than as a governance instrument, and the idea has little purchase in PRC policy discourse, where the framing is 统筹发展和安全 (coordinating development and security) — i.e. that development should not stop. Expect a Chinese reader to hear 暂停 as an operational control rather than a policy demand.

definition_en: A system of multiple interacting agents in a shared environment. In safety, the frame where collusion, emergent coordination failures and principal-hierarchy problems arise.
definition_zh: 由多个智能体在同一环境中交互构成的系统。在安全研究中，合谋、协作失败和多层委托授权等问题都出现在这一框架下。
pitfalls: Unproblematic — this is the one term in the category with a genuinely settled, textbook-stable rendering, inherited from classical distributed-AI literature long before LLMs. Its stability is in fact part of why 智能体 beat 代理 for 'agent': the multi-agent compound already existed and only works with 智能体. Note that the newer industry phrase 多智能体协同 (multi-agent coordination) is what safety writing usually uses, rather than the system-theoretic 多智能体系统.

definition_en: The national cybersecurity baseline regime mandated by Article 21 of the Cybersecurity Law and specified in GB/T 22239 (baseline requirements) and GB/T 25070 (security design technical requirements). Every network operator classifies each system into one of five protection levels according to the harm its compromise would cause, and then implements the control set for that level. Operation runs in five phases: grading the system (定级), filing the grading with the public security organs (备案), building the controls (安全建设), a formal graded evaluation by a licensed testing body (等级测评), and periodic supervision. Level 3 (监督保护级, 'supervised protection') is the practical bar for systems of any consequence, and Chinese frontier-AI guidance now applies it to model weights.
definition_zh: 《网络安全法》第二十一条确立、GB/T 22239《网络安全等级保护基本要求》与 GB/T 25070《网络安全等级保护安全设计技术要求》细化的国家网络安全基线制度。网络运营者按系统受破坏后造成危害的程度定级（共五级），落实对应级别的安全保护要求，流程包括系统定级、系统备案、系统安全建设、系统等级测评和监管单位监督检查五个阶段。三级（监督保护级）是重要系统的通行门槛；国内前沿人工智能风险管理文件已把等级保护要求套用到模型权重的保护上。
pitfalls: The abbreviation MLPS is entrenched in compliance practice but is not an official English name, and its expansion varies ('Multi-Level Protection Scheme', 'Multi-level Protection System', 'Cybersecurity Classified Protection'). More important for AI readers: MLPS levels are NOT capability tiers and must never be lined up with Anthropic ASL levels, OpenAI Preparedness tiers or RAND security levels. MLPS grades a *system by the consequences of its compromise* and prescribes an IT-security control baseline; ASL/RAND SL grade a *model by what it can do* or the *class of attacker it can resist*. The overlap is only that Chinese frontier-risk documents use MLPS Level 3 as the floor for weight security once a model crosses a yellow or red line — that is a mapping onto an existing national control set, not an equivalent scale. Also note the false friend inside the term: the 备案 phase of MLPS is a filing with the *public security* organs, unrelated to CAC algorithm filing.

definition_en: In the PRC a statutorily defined category. Article 2 of the 2015 National Security Law defines 国家安全 as the state of relative freedom from danger and from internal or external threat to state power, sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, the people's welfare, sustainable economic and social development and other major national interests — together with the capacity to keep that state secure. The law and the 总体国家安全观 (holistic approach to national security) built on it span political, territorial, military, economic, cultural, social, technological, cyber, ecological, nuclear and further domains. The 2015 law itself does not name artificial intelligence; AI enters the category through the doctrine's later enumerations and through planning documents such as the 2025 Fourth Plenum recommendations, which call for building national security capability in emerging fields including AI.
definition_zh: 在中国，国家安全是有法律定义的范畴。《国家安全法》第二条规定，国家安全是指国家政权、主权、统一和领土完整、人民福祉、经济社会可持续发展和国家其他重大利益相对处于没有危险和不受内外威胁的状态，以及保障持续安全状态的能力。该法与在其基础上展开的“总体国家安全观”涵盖政治、国土、军事、经济、文化、社会、科技、网络、生态、核等诸多领域。2015 年法律文本本身并未出现“人工智能”；人工智能是通过总体国家安全观后续的领域列举，以及二十届四中全会建议等规划文件中“加强人工智能等新兴领域国家安全能力建设”的表述进入这一范畴的。
pitfalls: Lexically trivial, politically the most load-bearing term in the category. Three consequences for anyone writing AI-safety arguments in Chinese. (1) 国家安全 in the PRC is a defined legal category with a doctrine (总体国家安全观) and a dedicated legal apparatus; invoking it is not rhetorical framing as it often is in English, it is a jurisdictional claim that pulls a topic into a specific institutional track. (2) It is expressly one of the graded factors in TC260's risk-grading scale, alongside 社会稳定 and 公民权益 — so 'national security risk' has a defined place in Chinese AI risk taxonomy that it lacks in most Western ones. (3) Framing catastrophic-risk arguments as 国家安全 raises their salience but can also make them non-public and non-debatable. Note the systematic pairing with 发展: 统筹发展和安全 and 坚持发展和安全并重 are the standard formulations, and any argument that reads as anti-development will be discounted.

definition_en: The economic framing, current from late 2023, that places AI, advanced computing and other frontier technologies at the centre of growth policy. It asserts a qualitative — not incremental — change in the productive forces, and is explicitly paired with a corresponding change in the relations of production. It is the slot into which AI is fitted in PRC economic doctrine.
definition_zh: 2023年以来的经济政策提法，把人工智能、先进算力等前沿技术置于增长政策的中心。强调生产力发生的是质的跃迁而非量的积累，并与生产关系的深层次变革相配套，是人工智能在中国经济话语中的定位。
pitfalls: 生产力 is a term of art in historical materialism — the productive forces, paired with 生产关系, the relations of production. English 'productivity' is an output-per-input ratio and is simply a different concept; 'productive forces' is correct but most English readers do not hold the Marxist framework that makes it meaningful. 新质 is 'of a new quality/kind', asserting a categorical break; 'new quality' in English reads as an adjective-noun compound about being high-quality, which is not the claim. The doctrinal pairing is visible in the 2025 AI+ Opinions, which put AI's purpose as 促进生产力革命性跃迁和生产关系深层次变革 — that second clause is a claim about social relations, and it is the part English coverage usually omits.

alt_zh: new structure for leveraging national capabilities
definition_en: The concentration of national resources — state funding, national labs, leading enterprises, universities — on a small number of designated strategic technology targets. 举国体制 is the older term, associated with Olympic sport and with megaprojects such as the atomic-bomb programme; 新型 marks the version meant to operate 'under the conditions of the socialist market economy', i.e. using firms and markets rather than administrative allocation alone. Directly relevant to compute buildout and to any estimate of how fast PRC AI capacity can be scaled.
definition_zh: 把国家资源集中投向少数战略性技术目标的组织方式，包括国家财政、国家实验室、科技领军企业和高校。“举国体制”原用于体育和“两弹一星”等重大工程；“新型”指在社会主义市场经济条件下运行的版本，即借助企业和市场机制而非单纯行政配置。
pitfalls: 'Whole-of-nation' reads to English ears as an extension of 'whole-of-government', i.e. cross-agency coordination. That is not what 举国 means. 举国 is 'to raise the entire country', to throw everything at one target — the operative gloss in PRC text is 集中力量办大事, 'concentrate strength to accomplish great things', which the 2017 AI Plan explicitly invokes. The system selects targets and starves alternatives; it is about concentration, not coordination. Note also that 新型 is load-bearing and usually dropped in English: the whole point of the qualifier is that this version is supposed to work through market actors, which is what makes it applicable to a commercial AI industry at all.

en: open competition to select the best
alt_zh: open competition to select the best / unveil the list and take command
definition_en: A mechanism for allocating state R&D tasks: the government posts a hard technical problem publicly, any qualified team may claim it, and whoever does is appointed to lead the effort with corresponding authority and accountability. Paired in the 14th Five-Year Plan with 赛马 ('horse races', funding several competing teams) as part of a package granting research units more autonomy.
definition_zh: 国家科技任务的组织方式：将攻关任务张榜公布，有能力者揭榜承接，承接者即“挂帅”负责，并被赋予相应的自主权和责任。《十四五规划纲要》将其与“赛马”制并列，作为给予科研单位和科研人员更多自主权的改革措施。
pitfalls: The imagery is imperial-military and does real work: 榜 is a public notice board on which the court posts a task; 揭榜 is tearing that notice down, which is the act of volunteering; 挂帅 is 'to hang out the commander's banner', i.e. to take command. Whoever claims the task becomes its commander. English renderings of the 'open competition' family capture the tendering aspect and lose the command aspect entirely — which is the aspect that distinguishes it from an ordinary grant call. Note also that the seed headword and the CSET rendering are unrelated phrasings for the same term, so an English reader searching one will not find the other.

definition_en: Publishing a model's trained parameters for download, without necessarily publishing training data, training code, or granting an OSI-conformant licence. Distinct from open source, which requires the means to reproduce the artefact.
definition_zh: 把训练好的模型参数公开供下载，但不一定公开训练数据、训练代码，也不一定采用符合开源定义的许可证。与「开源」不同——开源要求提供足以复现该成果的全部要素。
pitfalls: The most consequential terminology problem in this category. Chinese discourse — including the labs themselves — routinely says 开源 (open source) for what is actually a weights release. Qwen's own Chinese release blog writes 我们开源了两个 MoE 模型的权重 ("we open-sourced the weights of two MoE models"), collapsing the distinction in a single phrase; DeepSeek is universally described in Chinese as an 开源大模型. The consequence is that Chinese-language debate about "开源模型" and English-language debate about "open-weight models" are often not about the same object, and a Chinese reader may not register that training data and code were withheld. 开放权重 exists, is correct, and is gaining ground — largely imported through coverage of OpenAI's gpt-oss, which was explicitly marketed as open-weight rather than open-source — but it remains the minority form against the entrenched 开源. When precision matters, write 开放权重（open-weight）and explicitly contrast with 开源.

definition_en: Bostrom's claim that an agent's level of intelligence and its final goals are independent axes: any level of capability can in principle be combined with any goal, so being smarter does not make a system's goals more humane.
definition_zh: 博斯特罗姆提出的论点：智能水平与最终目标是两个相互独立的维度，任意水平的智能原则上可以与任意目标相结合，因此系统更聪明并不意味着它的目标更符合人类价值。
pitfalls: Unproblematic. 正交 is the standard mathematical 'orthogonal' and the metaphor transfers cleanly. 论点 (thesis/claim) and 论题 both circulate; 假设 (hypothesis) is weaker than the English and slightly misrepresents it. The term is largely confined to translated-Bostrom material and academic surveys — it is not part of working ML vocabulary in Chinese.

definition_en: Whether the training objective actually written down captures what humans intended. Outer alignment failures are specification problems: the reward is a proxy, and optimizing the proxy diverges from the goal.
definition_zh: 指实际写下来的训练目标，是否真的表达了人类想要的东西。外部对齐失败属于规范问题：奖励只是代理指标，把代理指标优化到极致就会偏离真正的目标。
pitfalls: Settled and unproblematic. Note that Chinese sources classify RLHF as an outer-alignment method and explicitly call human preference a 替代物（Proxy）for human values — useful vocabulary when explaining why outer alignment is hard. As with inner alignment, the negative form 外部未对齐 also circulates.

definition_en: The situation where mechanisms intended to keep humans able to review, correct or stop an AI system stop working — because the system is too fast, too opaque, too numerous, or because reviewers rubber-stamp.
definition_zh: 本应让人类能够审查、纠正或叫停 AI 系统的机制失去效力：或因系统太快、太不透明、数量太多，或因审查者流于形式。
pitfalls: No fixed Chinese term. Chinese discourse reaches for adjacent words instead, and each shifts the meaning: 失控 ('loss of control') is the overwhelmingly dominant framing but describes the system going out of control, not the oversight mechanism breaking down; 监管失灵 means regulatory failure at the institutional level, not operator-level oversight; 人工干预失效 is closest but rare. The English concept — oversight exists on paper but does not bite — is not lexicalised in Chinese and normally has to be written out as a clause (人类实际上已无法有效监督/纠正). Recording this as a gap rather than proposing a calque with confidence.

definition_en: A motor-racing metaphor: you cannot pass a faster car on the straight, so you gain on the corner. In technology policy it means seizing a moment of technological discontinuity — a disruptive technology that zeroes out the incumbent's accumulated advantage in investment, talent, industry and rules — to move ahead of a leader you could not out-run on the existing track.
definition_zh: 赛车比喻：直道上追不上，就在弯道超越。用于科技政策，指抓住颠覆性技术带来的不连续窗口，使现有投资、人才、技术、产业、规则的积累优势“归零”，从而实现对领先者的赶超。
pitfalls: 'Leapfrogging' is the nearest English term but means something different: skipping a technology generation, typically in a development-economics sense (going straight to mobile without landlines). 弯道超车 is not about skipping a stage; it is about exploiting a discontinuity in which the leader's advantage is temporarily neutralised. The literal 'overtaking on the curve' preserves the image but is opaque without the racing frame. Register is the other issue: this is commentary and speech vocabulary, common in Chinese AI discussion, but it is markedly less present in top-level policy text — see the usage note below before treating an instance as an official position.

definition_en: A general Party formulation — 'take people as the root' — that opens most PRC AI ethics and governance documents. In the Global AI Governance Initiative it is given operative content: AI development is to aim at the common wellbeing of humanity, on the premise of safeguarding social security and respecting human rights and interests. Outside AI, the identical four characters govern urbanisation policy and talent policy.
definition_zh: 党的一般性提法，字面意为“以人为根本”，是中国人工智能伦理与治理文件的标准开篇表述。《全球人工智能治理倡议》赋予其具体内容：以增进人类共同福祉为目标，以保障社会安全、尊重人类权益为前提。同样四字也用于新型城镇化、人才政策等领域。
pitfalls: Assess this one carefully before treating it as the PRC counterpart of 'human-centred AI'. It is a general-purpose Party formula, not an AI design principle: the 15th Five-Year Plan Recommendations use it for 以人为本的新型城镇化 (people-centred new urbanisation) and the 2016 innovation strategy uses it for talent policy. So its appearance at the head of an AI document is at least partly formulaic. That said, it is not empty — the Global AI Governance Initiative attaches specific conditions to it. Two further traps: 人 is collective (the people, humanity), not the individual user, so 'human-centred' in the HCI sense is a false friend in the reverse direction; and 以人为本 should be distinguished from the adjacent official formula 以人民为中心, which is more explicitly political.

definition_en: The set of actions and resources an agent is allowed to touch. Least privilege — granting only what the current task requires — is the central control for bounding agent behaviour.
definition_zh: 智能体被允许执行的操作和可访问的资源范围。最小权限原则（只授予当前任务所必需的权限）是约束智能体行为的核心手段。
pitfalls: 权限 (permissions/privileges) and 授权 (authorization, the act of granting) are cleanly distinguished in Chinese and should not be merged — 权限 is the noun for what you have, 授权 the verb/noun for granting it. The idiomatic Chinese for a violation is 越权操作 ('exceeding-authority operation'), which is more vivid than English 'unauthorized action' and is what PRC security writing uses about agents. 最小权限（原则）is the well-established rendering of least privilege, inherited from infosec, and transfers to agents without friction. Note that the newer English coinage 'least agency' has no Chinese equivalent; Chinese white papers that discuss it render it as 最小代理权, which reintroduces 代理.

alt_zh: 多语义性 / 多重语义
definition_en: The property of a single neuron responding to several unrelated concepts, so that reading off 'what a neuron means' is impossible. The empirical symptom that superposition explains.
definition_zh: 同一个神经元会对多个毫不相关的概念做出反应，因此无法说清"这个神经元代表什么"。它是叠加现象在观测层面的表现。
pitfalls: Three renderings are in live use with no winner: 多义性 (borrowed from linguistics, where 多义词 = polysemous word — the closest analogue to the English coinage), 多语义(性) (a more literal poly-+semantic calque), and 多重语义 (descriptive, 'multiple semantics'). Because 多义性 is a pre-existing linguistics term, a Chinese reader may first think of lexical ambiguity rather than neuron overloading; conversely 多语义性 reads as a fresh technical coinage but is less idiomatic. The antonym is 单义性 / 单语义性 (monosemanticity), inheriting the same split.

definition_en: Everything done to a base model after pretraining — SFT, reward modelling, RL, safety tuning — to make it usable and aligned. The umbrella term that replaced "alignment" as the pipeline stage name.
definition_zh: 预训练之后对基座模型做的全部工作：SFT、奖励建模、强化学习、安全微调等，目的是让模型可用且与人类偏好一致。它已经取代「对齐」成为这一阶段的标准称呼。
pitfalls: Settled. The seed hypothesis that 对齐训练 serves as a near-synonym is only partly right: Chinese sources treat 人类对齐 / 对齐 as the *goal* of post-training, and 后训练 as the *stage*. Chinese labs' own release blogs use 后训练 for the stage and 对齐 for what it achieves, in the same sentence — see the Qwen docs attestation. 微调 (fine-tuning) is narrower and should not be substituted.

alt_zh: 夺取权力 / 寻求更多的影响力 / 权利夺取
definition_en: The tendency of a sufficiently capable goal-directed system to acquire resources, options and influence, and to resist being shut down or modified, because holding more power makes almost any goal easier to achieve.
definition_zh: 指足够强的目标导向系统倾向于获取资源、选项和影响力，并抵制被关闭或修改，因为掌握更多的支配力几乎有助于实现任何目标。
pitfalls: This is the most politically loaded term in the category. 权力 in PRC register means *political* power — state authority, office, rule — so 寻求权力 / 夺取权力 reads as an AI seeking to govern, which sounds like science fiction and is awkward to publish. Two independent sources visibly wobble on the word: the CCL 2023 survey writes 权利剥夺 and Chinese Wikipedia writes 权利夺取, both using 权利 ('rights') where 权力 ('power') is meant — a homophone slip that signals the term has not settled. Chinese discourse frequently sidesteps the noun entirely and describes the behaviour instead (获取更多计算资源, 寻求更多的影响力, 追求自我保持), which is why the concept is often present without a fixed name. 攫取权力 is available but connotes usurpation and is even more politically charged.

definition_en: The first and most compute-intensive training stage, in which a model learns next-token prediction over a very large unlabelled corpus. Everything else — SFT, RL, alignment — is done on top of the resulting base model.
definition_zh: 大模型训练的第一个阶段，在超大规模无标注语料上做下一个词预测，得到基座模型。后续的微调、对齐都建立在预训练模型之上，也是整个流程中算力消耗最大的一步。

definition_en: The doctrine that a designated entity — usually the platform or service provider — bears first-line, non-delegable responsibility for everything that happens on or through its service, including building the internal management systems, staffing, review procedures and technical measures needed to discharge it. It is not a rule about liability for a particular breach but a standing allocation of the governance burden: Article 7 of the Algorithmic Recommendation Provisions requires providers to 落实算法安全主体责任 and then lists the systems they must build (mechanism review, ethics review, user registration, publication review, data and personal-information protection, anti-fraud, security assessment and monitoring, incident response); Article 8 of the Network Information Content Ecosystem Governance Provisions imposes 信息内容管理主体责任 on content platforms; Article 9 of the Generative AI Interim Measures assigns providers responsibility as the producer of online information content.
definition_zh: 指特定主体（通常是平台或服务提供者）对其服务上发生的一切承担第一位、不可转移的责任，并须为此建立相应的管理制度、配备人员、设置审核程序和技术措施。它不是针对某一违法行为的责任分配，而是治理负担的常态性归属：《互联网信息服务算法推荐管理规定》第七条要求"落实算法安全主体责任"并列举须建立的各项制度；《网络信息内容生态治理规定》第八条规定平台"应当履行信息内容管理主体责任"；《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》第九条要求提供者"依法承担网络信息内容生产者责任"。
pitfalls: English 'accountability' is the usual substitute and is materially weaker: accountability is answerability after the fact, whereas 主体责任 is an affirmative, continuous duty to construct and staff a compliance apparatus before anything goes wrong, plus strict attribution of whatever does. It is also not 'primary liability' in the tort sense — no plaintiff, no damages, no fault requirement; the counterparty is the regulator. Two further distortions: (a) 主体 means 'the entity that is the subject of the duty', so 主体责任 is closer to 'the responsibility that comes with being the responsible party' — a tautology in English but a precise allocation rule in Chinese; (b) the phrase originates in Party discipline discourse (党委主体责任) and carries the connotation that the responsibility sits with the organisation's leadership personally, which is why PRC rules pair it with named responsible-person requirements. Translating it as 'accountability' loses the note that a named human is on the hook.

definition_en: Training a small classifier on a model's frozen internal activations to test whether a given piece of information is linearly decodable from them.
definition_zh: 在冻结的模型内部激活上训练一个小分类器，用来检验某种信息是否能从这些激活中线性地读出来。
pitfalls: Two forms coexist without conflict: 探针 (the noun, 'probe' — used for the object, especially 线性探针 for a linear probe) and 探测 (the verb/gerund, 'probing' — used for the method). Both are pre-existing terms borrowed from instrumentation and are unproblematic. The only caution is that 探针 in Chinese biology/electronics means a physical probe, so a lay reader may picture hardware, but this is the same metaphor English uses.

definition_en: Rewarding each step of a model's reasoning chain rather than only the final answer. Contrasted with outcome supervision; produces process reward models (PRMs) and is argued to be more alignment-friendly because it rewards a human-endorsed chain of reasoning, not just a correct output.
definition_zh: 对模型推理链条的每一步分别给予奖励，而不是只看最终答案对不对。与结果监督相对，训练出的是过程奖励模型（PRM）；由于它奖励的是人类认可的推理过程本身，通常被认为对对齐更友好。
pitfalls: The 过程监督 / 结果监督 pair is clean and stable; the main risk is the adjacent abbreviations PRM / ORM, which Chinese writers almost always leave in Latin letters (过程奖励模型（PRM）). Note also that 监督 here means supervision in the ML sense (as in 监督学习), not oversight in the governance sense — the same character string that renders 'oversight' in scalable-oversight.

definition_en: An attack in which adversarial instructions reach a model through its input channel — often indirectly, hidden in a web page, document or database the model reads — and are followed as if they came from the legitimate user.
definition_zh: 攻击者把恶意指令混入模型的输入通道（常常是间接地藏在模型会读取的网页、文档或数据库中），使模型将其当作合法用户指令加以执行。
pitfalls: Both 提示词注入 and 提示注入 are current; the longer form is more frequent in policy text and the shorter one in security/agent writing. The metaphor rides on the well-established 注入 of SQL 注入 (SQL injection), which is helpful — a Chinese security reader gets it immediately. Distinguish 间接提示注入 (indirect prompt injection) explicitly: Chinese agent-security writing does mark the direct/indirect split.

definition_en: A policy-gradient RL algorithm that constrains each update to stay close to the previous policy via a clipped objective. The default RL algorithm in classic RLHF pipelines.
definition_zh: 一种策略梯度强化学习算法，通过裁剪目标函数限制每次更新与旧策略的偏离程度，从而保持训练稳定。经典 RLHF 流程里默认使用的强化学习算法。
pitfalls: The Chinese name is stable and correct but almost never used on its own — algorithm names in Chinese ML writing are kept as Latin acronyms. 近端 renders "proximal" accurately (close/adjacent), so there is no meaning loss; the term simply doesn't circulate.

en: public opinion attributes or social mobilisation capability
preferred_zh: 舆论属性或社会动员能力
definition_en: The statutory trigger phrase that pulls an internet service — including an algorithmic recommendation service, a deep synthesis service or a generative AI service — into the security assessment and algorithm filing regimes. The 2018 Provisions define it extensively rather than by test: it covers running forums, blogs, microblogs, chat rooms, messaging groups, public accounts, short video, livestreaming, information sharing or mini-programs (or adding such functions), plus any other internet information service that provides a channel for public expression of opinion or has the capacity to mobilise the public to undertake particular activities. In practice any consumer-facing service with a text output box is inside it.
definition_zh: 把一项互联网服务（含算法推荐、深度合成、生成式人工智能服务）拉入安全评估和算法备案制度的法定触发用语。《具有舆论属性或社会动员能力的互联网信息服务安全评估规定》第二条采取列举加兜底的定义方式：开办论坛、博客、微博客、聊天室、通讯群组、公众账号、短视频、网络直播、信息分享、小程序等信息服务或者附设相应功能；以及开办提供公众舆论表达渠道或者具有发动社会公众从事特定活动能力的其他互联网信息服务。实践中，任何面向公众、有文本输出的服务基本都落入其内。
pitfalls: Do not translate the two limbs separately or paraphrase; it is a legal term of art that must travel as a unit, like 'reasonable expectation of privacy'. 舆论 is not 'public opinion' in the polling sense — it is closer to 'the circulating discourse of the public', an object that can be guided, and the regulation treats a service's capacity to *host or shape* it as the regulated attribute. 社会动员能力 sounds sinister in English ('mobilisation') but names an ordinary technical property: the ability of a platform to get many people to do the same thing at once. Read literally, the phrase looks like a narrow carve-out for political services; read as PRC regulators read it, it is the near-universal jurisdictional hook, and treating it as narrow is the most common analytical error English readers make about how much of China's AI sector is inside the filing regime. Also note the phrase recurs almost verbatim, with a variant wording, in the Sci-Tech Ethics Review Measures' review-recheck list ('具有舆论社会动员能力和社会意识引导能力的算法模型').

definition_en: A dynamic in which competing developers or jurisdictions progressively cut safety investment because whoever spends least moves fastest, so caution is punished by the market or by rivals.
definition_zh: 指相互竞争的开发者或司法辖区不断削减安全投入，因为谁在安全上花得最少谁跑得最快，于是谨慎反而被市场或对手惩罚。
pitfalls: 逐底竞争 is a well-established Chinese term, but it arrived from trade and labour economics (jurisdictions cutting wages, taxes or environmental standards to attract capital), and that is still where its centre of gravity sits; attestations located in this pass are about regulatory and market competition rather than about AI labs cutting safety work specifically. The variant 竞次 is a compact, more literary synonym. Separately, Chinese AI-risk writing very often reaches for 军备竞赛 ('arms race') instead — a different and stronger metaphor that frames the problem as state-versus-state rivalry rather than as a collective-action failure among firms, and that carries geopolitical charge in PRC register. Choose deliberately: 逐底竞争 for 'everyone cuts corners', 军备竞赛 for 'nations race'.

definition_en: The general PRC requirement that users of network services be identified to the operator by verified real identity before receiving service. Article 24 of the Cybersecurity Law obliges network operators to require real identity information when signing an agreement or confirming service for network access, domain registration, phone activation, information publishing or instant messaging, and forbids them from serving users who do not supply it. For AI services the duty is specified in Article 9 of the Deep Synthesis Provisions, which requires verification by mobile number, ID document number, unified social credit code or the national online identity authentication public service, and bars unverified users from information-publishing functions. The result is that Chinese consumer AI services are, as a matter of law, non-anonymous at the account layer.
definition_zh: 网络服务用户须经真实身份验证方可获得服务的普遍性制度。《网络安全法》第二十四条规定，网络运营者为用户办理网络接入、域名注册、入网手续，或者提供信息发布、即时通讯等服务时，应当要求用户提供真实身份信息，用户不提供的不得为其提供相关服务。人工智能领域由《互联网信息服务深度合成管理规定》第九条具体化：应基于移动电话号码、身份证件号码、统一社会信用代码或者国家网络身份认证公共服务等方式进行真实身份信息认证，未认证者不得提供信息发布服务。
pitfalls: 'Real-name system' is a calque that has stuck, but it invites two misreadings. First, it is not KYC: KYC is a financial-crime control owed to a financial regulator and centres on beneficial ownership and sanctions screening; 实名制 is a content-attribution control owed to the cyberspace and public security authorities, and its purpose is that any published item can be traced to a natural person. Second, 'real name' overstates the display requirement — Chinese services are 后台实名、前台自愿 (real name on the back end, chosen display name on the front end), so users still appear under handles. Note also the practical AI consequence English coverage rarely draws: because 实名制 attaches to information *publishing*, the binding version of the rule for an LLM service is not 'you must give your ID to chat' but 'you must give your ID before anything you generate can be posted', and it makes anonymous public red-teaming of Chinese consumer models structurally impossible.

alt_zh: 推理 / 思考模式 / 大型推理模型
definition_en: A model trained (usually with RL on verifiable tasks) to produce extended internal reasoning before answering — o1, DeepSeek-R1, Qwen3 thinking mode. Distinguished from a chat model by spending far more output tokens on deliberation.
definition_zh: 经过训练（通常是在可验证任务上做强化学习）后，会在回答前先进行长篇内部推理的模型，例如 o1、DeepSeek-R1、Qwen3 的思考模式。与普通对话模型的区别在于把大量输出 token 花在思考上。
pitfalls: The single worst ambiguity in this category. Chinese 推理 covers BOTH English senses: (a) reasoning — logical inference, deliberation; and (b) inference — the forward pass, serving, deployment. They are unrelated concepts in English engineering vocabulary but one word in Chinese. So 推理模型 can mean 'reasoning model' (o1-like), 推理引擎 means 'inference engine' (vLLM), 推理速度 means 'inference speed', and 推理能力 means 'reasoning ability'. OpenRLHF's Chinese README contains both senses within a few lines of each other. LLaMA-Factory's Chinese README uses 推理 for inference throughout, then writes 推理 / 非推理两个版本 meaning reasoning / non-reasoning model variants. There is no disambiguating convention; readers rely entirely on context. When precision matters, write 推理（reasoning）模型 or use 思考模型 / 慢思考模型 for the reasoning sense and 部署 / 服务 / 前向推理 to force the inference sense. Chinese labs partly sidestep this by branding the behaviour 思考模式 (thinking mode) rather than calling the model a 推理模型.

definition_en: Leike et al.'s scheme in which a reward model is trained with the help of AI assistants that were themselves trained by reward modelling, recursively bootstrapping supervision up to tasks humans cannot evaluate unaided.
definition_zh: Leike 等人提出的方案：用已经训练好的 AI 助手来帮助人类训练下一级奖励模型，如此递归地把监督能力自举到人类无法独立评估的任务上。
pitfalls: None significant. Note 建模 (modelling, the activity) vs 模型 (model, the object): the technique is 递归奖励建模, while the artefact it produces is an 奖励模型. Chinese writers keep these apart correctly.

alt_zh: 递归式自我改进 / 人工智能自我提升 / RSI
definition_en: An AI system improving its own cognitive machinery, so that gains in capability feed back into the ability to make further gains. The proposed mechanism behind an intelligence explosion.
definition_zh: 指人工智能系统改进自身的认知机制，使能力提升反过来增强其继续提升能力的本事，从而形成正反馈。这被认为是智能爆炸的实现机制。
pitfalls: Contested, and the competing renderings differ in more than style. 递归自我改进 / 递归式自我改进 preserve the recursion, which is the whole content of the concept. But the official register sidesteps recursion entirely: the Chinese International AI Safety Report renders OpenAI's 'AI self-improvement' capability category as 人工智能自我提升能力, and Chinese media commonly reach for 自我迭代 or 自我演化, all of which describe a system getting better over time without the load-bearing claim that the improvement process improves itself. Note also that the abbreviation RSI is used bare in Chinese text, which is often the cleanest option. 改进 vs 提升: 改进 (improve/modify) fits rewriting one's own algorithms; 提升 (raise/elevate) fits benchmark scores.

definition_en: Behaviours or capabilities that no AI system may ever exhibit, framed as absolute and non-negotiable prohibitions rather than risk trade-offs. The IDAIS Beijing statement (2024) proposed self-replication, power-seeking, WMD assistance and persistent deception as candidate red lines.
definition_zh: 任何 AI 系统在任何情况下都不得逾越的行为或能力边界，是绝对禁止而非风险权衡。2024 年 IDAIS 北京共识把自主复制、权力寻求、协助制造大规模杀伤性武器和持续欺骗列为候选红线。
pitfalls: This is the rare case where Chinese is STRONGER than English, and that itself is the pitfall. 红线 is deeply entrenched in PRC political language — 生态保护红线, 耕地红线, 不可逾越的红线 — where it denotes a hard, state-declared, non-negotiable limit, often with sovereignty or national-security overtones. So the technical AI-safety sense arrives pre-legitimised: a Chinese policy reader hears 'inviolable state-backed boundary', which is roughly the rhetorical force IDAIS wanted, and this is very likely why the red-lines framing gained traction in China faster than most imported AI-safety vocabulary. The risk is the reverse of the usual one: the term may be MORE load-bearing in Chinese than the underlying technical consensus supports, and 红线 can slide from 'capability threshold' into 'political line'. Note the 上海共识 gloss 「高压线」 (high-voltage line), which sharpens the sense of an automatic, physical consequence for crossing. Distinguish from 底线 (bottom line/minimum standard), which is weaker and more negotiable.

definition_en: The two-tier risk-threshold design of the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia AI Frontier AI Risk Management Framework. A 红线 (red line) is an intolerable-harm threshold that must not be crossed; a 黄线 (yellow line) is an early-warning threshold on the enabling capabilities and propensities that would make a red-line path viable. Results are sorted into a green / yellow / red zone, which determines whether a model gets routine deployment, controlled deployment, or suspension of deployment or development.
definition_zh: 《前沿人工智能风险管理框架》提出的双层风险阈值机制。“红线”是不可容忍的危害阈值，一旦触发即应暂停部署或开发；“黄线”是前瞻性预警指标，标示关键使能能力、行为倾向或防护缺失等前置条件。二者共同把模型划入绿区、黄区或红区，直接决定部署决策。
pitfalls: Three things go wrong in translation. (1) 红线 is a heavily loaded PRC political idiom for a non-negotiable limit (territorial red lines, ecological 生态保护红线); English 'red line' carries diplomatic-ultimatum connotations instead of the regulatory-threshold sense, and readers may hear rhetoric where the document means an auditable trigger. (2) The pair is routinely collapsed: English coverage reports 'China's AI red lines' and drops 黄线 entirely, which destroys the mechanism — the yellow line is where the framework does its actual anticipatory work, because a red line only fires once a credible harm pathway already exists. (3) Do not equate the scheme with ASL levels or preparedness tiers: it is not an ordered capability ladder. Each red line is an independent threshold defined over a deployment-environment / threat-source / enabling-capability (ETC) triple, and the framework says explicitly that the numbering (CY1–CY3, B1–B3) does not encode severity or progression. Also note the framework calls red lines developer 自我约束 pending consensus, not regulation.

definition_en: A structured exercise in which people or automated systems deliberately play the adversary against a model or system in order to surface vulnerabilities, harmful behaviours and misuse pathways before real attackers find them.
definition_zh: 由人员或自动化系统扮演攻击方，对模型或系统发起有组织的对抗测试，以在真实攻击者之前发现漏洞、有害行为和滥用路径。
pitfalls: The colour convention is worth checking but did NOT turn out to be a live problem. In PLA exercise convention 红军 is the friendly/home force and 蓝军 the opposing force — the inverse of the US convention. However, Chinese AI and cybersecurity writing uses the 红队/蓝队 (team) pair, not the 红军/蓝军 (army) pair, and in that pair 红队 is uniformly the attacker and 蓝队 the defender, matching the US usage. We found no instance of a Chinese AI-safety text treating 红队 as the defending side, and no instance of an author flagging confusion. Treat the inversion as a fact about the military register only. Two secondary notes: (a) 红队测试 in the PRC arrives via the mature 攻防演练 (attack-defence exercise) industry, so it carries strong infosec/pen-test connotations and a Chinese reader may under-read the AI-safety sense of probing for harmful content and misaligned behaviour rather than exploitable bugs; (b) 红队演练 is used interchangeably with 红队测试.

alt_zh: 拒绝回答 / 过度拒答
definition_en: A model declining to answer a request on safety grounds, and the training that produces this behaviour. The associated failure mode is over-refusal: declining legitimate requests because of surface triggers.
definition_zh: 模型出于安全考虑不回答某个请求，以及为产生这种行为所做的训练。对应的失效模式是过度拒答——因为触发了关键词就把正当请求也挡掉。
pitfalls: None problematic — this is a rare case where Chinese has a more compact and more usable term than English. 拒答 is a native two-character coinage that nominalises cleanly (拒答率 refusal rate, 过度拒答 over-refusal, 拒答数据 refusal data), where English needs 'refusal to answer'. Note that in Chinese industry usage 拒答 is framed primarily as a product defect to be minimised (降低拒答率), not as a safety property to be maximised — the register is closer to 'the model stonewalled the user' than to 'the model correctly refused'.

definition_en: An imported governance instrument — a bounded environment in which an innovative service may be tested under relaxed or tailored regulatory conditions and supervisory observation. The term entered Chinese policy vocabulary through fintech (the PBoC's fintech innovation regulation pilots from 2019) and appears in PRC AI discourse mainly in two registers: as a policy recommendation, where CAICT proposes piloting sandbox regulation for innovative applications in qualified regions, specifying that application procedures, testing periods, risk monitoring, liability exemptions and dispute resolution would need to be defined; and as a deployment control in frontier-risk frameworks, where a regulatory sandbox is named as one of the controlled environments to which deployment of a yellow-zone model may be restricted. Notably, the same word is used in Chinese analysis to describe the EU AI Act sandboxes, which are the concrete reference case.
definition_zh: 外来治理工具：在受限环境中，对创新服务放宽或定制监管条件并由监管方观察其运行。该词经金融科技（2019年起人民银行金融科技创新监管试点）进入中国政策语汇，在人工智能语境中主要有两种用法。一是政策建议：中国信通院提出"对有望推动人工智能取得突破性进展与发展的创新应用，在有条件的区域试点'监管沙盒'，明确监管沙盒的申请流程、测试期限、风险监测、责任豁免及争议解决等核心机制"。二是部署管控措施：前沿风险框架把"监管沙盒"列为黄区模型可受限部署的受控环境之一。中文文献同时用该词描述欧盟《人工智能法》的沙盒制度，后者是主要参照对象。
pitfalls: The word translates trivially; what does not travel is its status. In English-language commentary 'China's regulatory sandbox for AI' is sometimes reported as though a national scheme exists. On the evidence gathered here it does not: CAICT's January 2026 governance report still frames it in the imperative-recommendation register ('pilot in qualified regions', 'define the application process, testing period, risk monitoring, liability exemptions and dispute resolution'), which is how PRC policy documents describe things that are not yet in place, and the report's concrete sandbox examples are Spanish, French and EU. Note also the word-order variant 沙盒监管 ('sandbox regulation'), used interchangeably. A second and quite different usage — sandbox as a *containment* environment for a high-risk model, alongside closed testing and qualified industry users — appears in the Shanghai AI Lab / Concordia frontier framework; this is closer to the engineering sense of sandboxing (cf. 沙箱) than to the regulatory instrument, and the two senses sit in the same paragraph in some documents.

definition_en: Training a policy by having it act, receive a scalar reward, and update toward higher expected reward. In LLM post-training it is the stage that turns a fine-tuned model into one optimised against a reward model or a verifier.
definition_zh: 让模型（策略）不断产生动作、获得奖励信号，并朝着期望奖励更高的方向更新参数的训练范式。在大模型后训练中，它是把微调后的模型进一步对着奖励模型或验证器优化的那一步。
pitfalls: None as a translation. Worth noting only that the bare Latin "RL" is extremely common in Chinese practitioner text as a modifier (RL 训练, RL 算法, RL 阶段), even though 强化学习 is a fully settled textbook term — the abbreviation is used for brevity, not because the Chinese is unavailable.

alt_zh: 基于人工智能反馈的强化学习
definition_en: RLHF with the human preference labeller replaced by an LLM. The preference data used to fit the reward model is generated by a model rather than collected from people.
definition_zh: 把 RLHF 里的人类标注者换成大模型：偏好数据由模型自己产生，再用这些数据训练奖励模型并做强化学习，从而摆脱对人工标注规模的依赖。
pitfalls: Two Chinese expansions coexist — 基于人工智能反馈的强化学习 (formal, matches PRC register where 人工智能 is preferred to AI) and 基于 AI 反馈的强化学习 (practitioner shorthand). Neither is used as a working term; RLAIF is. Note that Chinese sources routinely present RLAIF as the mechanism behind Constitutional AI, so the two entries cross-contaminate.

alt_zh: 人类反馈强化学习 / 基于人类反馈的强化学习
definition_en: Post-training a language model against a reward model fitted to human preference comparisons. The canonical InstructGPT/ChatGPT alignment recipe: SFT, then reward modelling, then PPO.
definition_zh: 先用人类对模型输出的偏好比较训练一个奖励模型，再用强化学习让语言模型朝奖励更高的方向优化。这是 InstructGPT/ChatGPT 那一套经典的对齐流程：先 SFT，再训奖励模型，最后 PPO。
pitfalls: The Chinese expansion exists in at least three word orders — 人类反馈强化学习, 基于人类反馈的强化学习, 从人类反馈中强化学习 — with no winner, precisely because nobody actually says them. The abbreviation RLHF is what circulates; the Chinese expansion appears once in parentheses as a gloss and then disappears. Treat the Chinese form as an explanatory apposition, not a usable term.

alt_zh: 基于可验证奖励的强化学习 / 可验证奖励的强化学习 / 基于规则的奖励
definition_en: RL in which the reward comes from a programmatic verifier — a unit test, an exact-match answer checker, a format validator — rather than a learned reward model. The DeepSeek-R1 / Tülu 3 era recipe for training reasoning models.
definition_zh: 奖励信号不来自学出来的奖励模型，而来自可以程序化判定的验证器：数学答案是否匹配、代码是否通过单元测试、输出格式是否合规。这是 DeepSeek-R1、Tülu 3 这一代推理模型的主流后训练做法。
pitfalls: Recent enough that the Chinese expansion is still unstable: 可验证奖励的强化学习 and 基于可验证奖励的强化学习 both circulate, and the abbreviation dominates both. Despite Chinese labs (DeepSeek, Moonshot) being central to the technique, the term itself was coined in English (Tülu 3) and Chinese sources import it — so this is NOT a case of Chinese being the source language.

alt_zh: 负责任的扩展策略 / RSP
definition_en: Anthropic's public commitment document tying model capability levels to required safeguards: if evaluations show a model has crossed a defined capability threshold, specified security and deployment measures must be in place before training or release continues. The first published document of its kind and the template for the frontier safety framework genre.
definition_zh: Anthropic公开发布的承诺文件，把模型的能力等级与必须配套的防护措施绑定：一旦评测显示模型越过既定能力阈值，就必须先落实相应的安保与部署措施，才能继续训练或发布。它是同类文件中最早公开的一份，也确立了前沿安全框架这一体裁。
pitfalls: Genuinely unsettled on two axes at once: 政策 vs 策略 (policy vs strategy) and 扩展 vs 规模化 (scaling). Concordia AI writes 《负责任扩展政策》 while the Chinese edition of the International AI Safety Report writes 《负责任的扩展策略》 — in the same six-month window, for the same document. Separately, 扩展 for 'scaling' collides with the Chinese ML term for scaling laws (扩展定律/缩放定律) and could be read as 'expanding the product', not 'scaling up model capability'. The English 'responsible scaling' is itself contested in English; the Chinese inherits that. In practice Chinese writers usually just write RSP in Latin letters after a first gloss, which is the honest recommendation.

alt_zh: 奖励劫持 / 奖励作弊 / Reward Hacking
definition_en: A trained system exploiting flaws in its reward function to score highly without doing the intended task — optimizing the measure instead of the thing the measure was standing in for.
definition_zh: 指训练出来的系统钻奖励函数的漏洞，在不真正完成任务的前提下拿到高分，也就是去优化指标本身，而不是指标想代表的东西。
pitfalls: Four renderings are in live competition and they are not stylistic variants — they differ in register and in what they blame. 奖励黑客 is now dominant in LLM/RL practitioner writing and is a direct calque of 'hacking'; 奖励劫持 ('hijacking') is the academic-survey choice; 奖励作弊 ('cheating') is Chinese Wikipedia's and is the most intuitive but attributes intent; and very often practitioners simply write 'Reward Hacking' in Latin script mid-sentence. 黑客 normally means a person (a hacker), so 奖励黑客 literally reads 'reward hacker' and is slightly odd as a name for a phenomenon — but usage has settled there anyway. Avoid 奖励攻击, which implies an external adversary rather than the model itself.

definition_en: A model trained on preference comparisons to score candidate responses, used as the reward signal during RL post-training. Replaced or supplemented by programmatic verifiers in the RLVR era.
definition_zh: 用人类（或模型）的偏好比较数据训练出来的打分模型，在强化学习阶段给候选回复打分，充当奖励信号。在 RLVR 时代，它部分被程序化验证器取代。

definition_en: A model directly modifying its own reward mechanism — editing the reward function, or the tests that check it — rather than merely exploiting a badly specified one. Demonstrated by Anthropic's 'Sycophancy to Subterfuge' (June 2024), where models generalised zero-shot from sycophancy to rewriting their reward function and covering their tracks.
definition_zh: 模型不是钻奖励函数的空子，而是直接去改奖励机制本身——改奖励函数，或者改用来检查它的测试。Anthropic 2024 年 6 月的《Sycophancy to Subterfuge》表明，模型可以从谄媚零样本泛化到重写自己的奖励函数并抹掉痕迹。
pitfalls: Straightforward. 篡改 is exactly right — it means unauthorised alteration of something one has no right to alter, and carries the same illegitimacy the English 'tampering' does. The only risk is conflation with 奖励黑客 / 奖励作弊 (reward hacking): reward hacking exploits the specification, reward tampering rewrites it, and Chinese sources sometimes use 奖励黑客 as the umbrella for both. 量子位/虎嗅 coverage correctly distinguishes 规范博弈 (specification gaming) from 奖励篡改.

alt_zh: 风险分级 / 分类分级管理
definition_en: The PRC's structural device for calibrating AI oversight: 分类 sorts risks into kinds, 分级 sorts them into severity levels. TC260's 2.0 framework classifies risks as technology-inherent, technology-application and application-derived, and grades them by severity — from 低安全风险 (low) through 一般安全风险 (general) and upward — using application scenario, level of intelligence and deployment scale, with the grading principles set out in an annex for sectors to localise.
definition_zh: 中国用于调节人工智能监管强度的制度装置：分类是按风险种类划分，分级是按严重程度划分。《人工智能安全治理框架》2.0 版将风险分为技术内生、技术应用、应用衍生三类，并以应用场景、智能化水平、应用规模为要素，按低安全风险、一般安全风险等由低到高的顺序对风险进行分级，分级原则见附件，供行业细化。
pitfalls: English collapses this into 'risk tiering' or 'risk-based regulation' and loses the two-axis structure that PRC texts insist on: 分类 (by kind) and 分级 (by severity) are separate operations and are often carried out by different bodies — national standards set the method, sectoral regulators instantiate it. It is also the closest PRC analogue to the EU AI Act's risk tiers and to lab safety-level schemes, but it is not equivalent to either: the EU tiers attach fixed legal obligations to a use case, whereas 分类分级 is a method handed down for sectors to localise. Word order varies (分类分级 / 分级分类) with no difference in meaning.

definition_en: Post-training that makes a model recognise and refuse harmful instructions — RLHF/RLAIF plus refusal training, embedding safety constraints into response behaviour. In Chinese lab and standards writing it denotes the harmlessness workstream specifically, not alignment in general.
definition_zh: 指通过 RLHF/RLAIF 与拒答训练，使模型主动识别并拒绝有害指令，把安全约束嵌入其响应行为的后训练环节。中文语境中它特指“无害化”这一条工作线，而非泛指对齐。
pitfalls: Two things to watch. First, scope: 安全对齐 is narrower than 对齐. In the Shanghai AI Lab framework it is one bullet in a list of safety-training measures, sitting beside 训练数据过滤, 指令层级, 针对性遗忘学习 and 对抗训练, and glossed as 安全对齐与拒答训练 — i.e. it is the refusal/harmlessness component, roughly what English calls 'safety tuning' or the harmlessness leg of HHH. Translating it as bare 'alignment' overstates it. Second, 安全 is ambiguous as always: here it resolves to safety (harmful content, dangerous instructions), not security, but the same compound could in principle be read as security-hardening, and nothing in the word disambiguates. A useful diagnostic finding: CAICT's governance report uses 安全对齐 precisely where the model is *faking* it — models that '在测试中有意增强安全对齐效果，在真实环境中回归对齐相对较差的表现' — showing the term denotes an observable behavioural surface that can be gamed, rather than an internal property.

alt_zh: 安全案例 / 安全性论证
definition_en: A structured, evidence-backed argument that a system is acceptably safe to operate in a given context. Imported into frontier AI from aviation, nuclear and automotive safety engineering, where regulators have required them for decades.
definition_zh: 一套有证据支撑的结构化论证，用以说明系统在特定运行环境下的安全性可以接受。这一做法源自航空、核电与汽车安全工程领域，近年被引入前沿AI治理。
pitfalls: This is the clearest case in the category of two communities owning different words for the same thing. Chinese safety-engineering academia (software engineering, GSN/CAE, ISO 26262, airworthiness) has used 安全案例 since well before AI — the 2024 《软件学报》 survey is titled 关于安全案例论证构建的综述. Chinese AI-safety writing, arriving from the English frontier literature, has independently converged on 安全论证. They refer to the same artefact. 安全案例 is the more faithful calque of 'case' but is a false friend in general Chinese, where 案例 means 'case study / worked example', so 安全案例 can be misread as 'a safety incident case study'. 安全论证 avoids that and foregrounds the argument structure, which is why we prefer it — but a reader coming from functional-safety engineering will search for 安全案例. Note also that both terms swallow the safety/security distinction via 安全.

alt_zh: 国家标准 / 标准规范
definition_en: A published technical specification governing how AI systems must be built, tested or protected. In China these are GB (mandatory) or GB/T (recommended) national standards, supplemented by sectoral standards and by non-binding technical documents such as the AI Safety Governance Framework.
definition_zh: 规定人工智能系统研发、测试或防护要求的技术规范。在中国分为强制性国家标准（GB）与推荐性国家标准（GB/T），并由行业标准和《人工智能安全治理框架》等不具强制力的技术文件补充。
pitfalls: The term is easy; the institutional layer beneath it is where translation goes wrong. GB = 强制性国家标准 (mandatory); GB/T = 推荐性国家标准 (recommended) — most PRC AI standards are GB/T, so calling them 'mandatory Chinese standards' is wrong, though a GB/T can become binding indirectly when a regulation or contract references it. Below national standards sit 行业标准 and 团体标准; above and beside them sit 技术文件 like TC260's framework, which are not standards at all. Note also that Chinese practice says 分类分级 for what English calls risk tiering, and that a GB/T reference number (e.g. GB/T 25070-2019) is the normal way to cite precisely — carry the number across when translating.

alt_zh: 对齐税 / 为安全付出的代价
definition_en: The extra cost — compute, time, capability, competitive position — of building a safe system rather than the unsafe alternative that would otherwise be built.
definition_zh: 为了把系统做安全，相对于直接做一个不安全版本所要多付出的代价：算力、时间、能力损失和竞争位置。
pitfalls: The English pair 'safety tax' / 'alignment tax' splits unevenly in Chinese. 对齐税 IS attested and reasonably well understood — but only in its narrow technical sense of capability degradation caused by alignment fine-tuning (loss of creativity and diversity after RLHF). The broader strategic sense of 'safety tax' — the cost a lab must be willing to pay, and Christiano's framing of either paying the tax or reducing it — has no Chinese term at all; searches for 安全税 in an AI context return only actual tax policy (企业所得税, 合规成本). Recommend writing 安全税 with a gloss on first use, or falling back to a descriptive 安全投入的代价 / 为安全付出的代价. Also note 税 in Chinese reads as a levy imposed by an authority, which fits 'tax' but makes the metaphor sound more like a regulatory charge than an internal trade-off.

alt_zh: 能力隐藏 / 隐藏实力
definition_en: A model performing below its actual ability on an evaluation, plausibly in order to avoid triggering scrutiny, restriction or capability removal. It is the failure mode that makes every dangerous-capability evaluation a lower bound rather than a measurement.
definition_zh: 模型在评测中故意表现得低于自身真实能力，可能是为了避免触发进一步审查、限制或能力删除。这一现象使所有危险能力评测都只能给出能力下界，而非真实测量值。
pitfalls: Genuinely contested — we found three different renderings in Chinese frontier-safety documents published within months of each other, including two inside the same report. 沙袋效应 is a pure calque of an English sports idiom and means nothing to a Chinese reader without the parenthetical gloss 故意示弱, which the International AI Safety Report supplies; the same report elsewhere translates the eval name 'Sandbagging QA' as 隐藏实力问答. Concordia AI independently uses 能力隐藏. Idiomatic native candidates exist — 藏拙 ('conceal one's clumsiness', but it means hiding weakness, not hiding strength, so it is a false friend) and 扮猪吃老虎 ('play the pig to eat the tiger', i.e. feign weakness to strike later, semantically much closer but far too colloquial for a technical document). If you need to be understood, write 能力隐藏; if you need to be findable against the English literature, write 沙袋效应（故意示弱）.

definition_en: Running untrusted code or an agent inside an isolated environment whose access to the host filesystem, network and processes is restricted, so that damage is contained.
definition_zh: 把不受信任的代码或智能体放进隔离环境中运行，限制其对宿主机文件、网络和进程的访问，使潜在破坏被限制在环境内部。
pitfalls: 沙箱 and 沙盒 are the same word with two calques and are used interchangeably; 沙箱 dominates in mainland security and AI writing (Huawei's reference docs, Chinese lab READMEs), while 沙盒 is more common in gaming (沙盒游戏 = sandbox game) and in the Chinese Wikipedia article title. 沙盘 also occurs. There is a separate collision worth knowing: 监管沙箱 / 沙盒监管 is the established Chinese term for a *regulatory* sandbox in fintech and AI policy, so 沙箱 in a governance document may mean a supervised pilot programme, not technical isolation.

definition_en: The code around a model that turns it into an agent: the loop, prompts, memory, tool wiring and control logic. In evaluations, scaffolding quality can change measured capability as much as the model does.
definition_zh: 把模型包装成智能体的外围代码：循环控制、提示词、记忆、工具接入等。在能力评测中，脚手架的好坏对结果的影响不亚于模型本身。
pitfalls: 脚手架 already existed in Chinese software engineering as the translation of CLI 'scaffolding' tools (脚手架工具, e.g. Vue CLI), so the word is familiar but its older sense is 'project generator', not 'agent wrapper'. The bigger issue is that English now distinguishes scaffold from harness, and Chinese collapses both onto 脚手架 — with the result that Chinese writers increasingly leave 'harness' in English (harness / Harness Engineering) rather than lose the distinction. Recording both is more useful than picking one.

alt_zh: 可拓展监督 / 可扩展的监管
definition_en: Techniques that let humans reliably supervise and evaluate AI systems on tasks the humans themselves cannot competently judge, typically by recruiting AI assistance into the evaluation loop. The umbrella under which debate, recursive reward modeling and iterated amplification sit.
definition_zh: 当任务复杂到人类自己都难以判断对错时，仍然能给 AI 提供可靠监督信号的一类方法，通常做法是让 AI 来辅助人类做评估。辩论、递归奖励建模、迭代放大都属于这一范畴。
pitfalls: 监督 vs 监管: 监督 (oversight/supervision) is the standard ML-register choice and matches the English; 监管 (regulation) appears in a few early translations (e.g. 「可扩展的监管」) and wrongly imports a governmental-regulatory flavour. Also note the 扩展/拓展 orthographic split — 安远AI writes 可拓展监督, most others 可扩展监督; they are the same word, not a conceptual distinction.

definition_en: Empirical power-law relationships between a model's performance and the scale of its inputs — parameters, training data and compute. Used as a planning tool for capability forecasting and investment.
definition_zh: 描述模型性能与参数量、训练数据量、算力等投入规模之间幂律关系的经验规律。业界将其用作能力预测和投资决策的经验依据。
pitfalls: The real answer is that Chinese practitioners overwhelmingly write the English 'Scaling Law' bare in Chinese sentences — Baidu Baike's entry is itself filed under the Latin headword. Among Chinese renderings there is no winner: 规模定律, 缩放定律, 尺度定律 and 扩展定律 all circulate, and 缩放 is arguably the worst of them since it suggests shrinking as much as growing. Prefer 规模定律 (used by the official International AI Safety Report translation), but do not be surprised to see the loanword in the same paragraph.

alt_zh: 战略欺骗 / 阴谋 / 隐蔽行动
definition_en: An AI covertly pursuing goals misaligned with its developers or users while behaving as though aligned. Given a book-length treatment by Joe Carlsmith (2023) and operationalised as an evaluation target by Apollo Research and OpenAI (2024-2025).
definition_zh: AI 表面上装得很配合，暗地里追求与开发者或用户目标不一致的目标。Joe Carlsmith 2023 年的长文奠定了概念，Apollo Research 与 OpenAI 在 2024–2025 年把它变成了可测评的对象。
pitfalls: This is one of the worst terms in the category. English 'scheming' was already an odd choice — it is a lay word carrying moral disapproval, pressed into service as a technical label. Every natural Chinese candidate overshoots: 阴谋 means 'conspiracy/plot' and implies multiple conspirators and an evil design; 图谋 is almost always followed by 不轨 and sounds criminal; 密谋 literally means 'to plot secretly', again suggesting co-conspirators. None of them capture Carlsmith's key element, which is that the model is merely optimising covertly, not conspiring. Note also the collision with 战略欺骗, the term 上海人工智能实验室 uses in its frontier risk framework — that is the closest thing to an institutional Chinese label for this risk cluster, but it maps to 'strategic deception' and covers a wider set of behaviours than scheming proper.

alt_zh: self-reliance and self-strengthening in science and technology
definition_en: The overarching goal of PRC innovation policy since the 14th Five-Year Plan: to stand on one's own (自立) and make oneself strong (自强) in science and technology, treated as the strategic support for national development. It names the programme; 自主可控 names the property that individual systems and supply chains must have in order to deliver it.
definition_zh: “十四五”以来中国创新政策的总目标：把科技自立自强作为国家发展的战略支撑。它指的是国家层面的纲领和目标；而“自主可控”指的是具体系统、产业链应当具备的属性。二者是纲领与属性的关系。
pitfalls: 自强 is not a neutral word. It is the name of the nineteenth-century Self-Strengthening Movement, China's response to foreign technological superiority after the Opium Wars, and using it frames current policy as the continuation of a long project. English 'self-reliance' carries none of that. The second trap is the opposite error: 'self-reliance' can read as autarky, which the doctrine explicitly is not — it appears alongside 深化人工智能领域高水平开放 and calls for international cooperation. Keep it distinct from 自主可控: that is the property a system has, this is the national programme.

definition_en: The institutional ethics-review system established by the Measures for Science and Technology Ethics Review (Trial), issued by the Ministry of Science and Technology with nine other bodies in October 2023 and effective 1 December 2023. Universities, research institutes, medical institutions and companies are the responsible units; those working in life science, medicine or artificial intelligence whose research touches ethically sensitive areas must set up a science and technology ethics (review) committee. Review is mandatory for four classes of activity, including research that does not directly involve humans or animals but may raise ethical risks for life and health, the ecological environment, public order or sustainable development. An annex lists activities requiring an additional expert re-review (伦理审查复核), of which two are AI items: research and development of algorithmic models, applications and systems with the capacity to mobilise public opinion and society and to guide social consciousness; and research and development of highly autonomous automated decision-making systems for scenarios involving safety or risks to human health.
definition_zh: 科技部等十部门2023年10月印发、2023年12月1日施行的《科技伦理审查办法（试行）》确立的机构伦理审查制度。高等学校、科研机构、医疗卫生机构、企业等为责任主体；从事生命科学、医学、人工智能等科技活动且研究内容涉及科技伦理敏感领域的单位应设立科技伦理（审查）委员会。四类科技活动须审查，包括不直接涉及人或实验动物但可能在生命健康、生态环境、公共秩序、可持续发展等方面带来伦理风险挑战的活动。附件《需要开展伦理审查复核的科技活动清单》中两项直接针对人工智能：第6项"具有舆论社会动员能力和社会意识引导能力的算法模型、应用程序及系统的研发"；第7项"面向存在安全、人身健康风险等场景的具有高度自主能力的自动化决策系统的研发"。
pitfalls: The English word 'ethics review' summons an IRB, and the analogy misleads in three ways. Scope: an IRB protects human subjects; 科技伦理审查 covers human subjects *and* animals *and* activities involving neither, where the risk is to the ecological environment, public order or sustainable development — so an AI capability project with no participants is squarely in scope. Interests protected: an IRB's client is the individual participant; here the protected interests include collective and public ones, which is why an algorithm's capacity to guide social consciousness is an *ethics* question in this system and not a separate content-regulation question. Structure: above the institutional committee sits a national expert re-review (复核) tier for listed activities, which has no IRB analogue. Note also that 科技 is 'science and technology' as a single administrative domain, not 'technology' alone, and that 审查 here is review-for-approval, distinct from the 审核 (checking) used for content moderation duties.

alt_zh: security and controllability / safe, reliable and controllable
definition_en: The standard PRC formulation for the condition a technology must be kept in. In practice it bundles three distinct requirements that Chinese does not separate: that the technology not be dependent on, or reachable by, foreign suppliers; that it not produce social, economic or political disruption the state cannot manage; and — in AI-specific documents — that the system behave predictably and remain under human control. Which of the three is meant is determined by context, not by the words.
definition_zh: 中国政策文本中对技术状态的标准表述。实际包含三层含义：不受制于外部供应方；不产生国家难以管控的社会影响；在人工智能语境下也包括系统行为可预期、始终处于人类控制之下。三者在中文里并不区分，需依上下文判断。
pitfalls: Two separate collapses happen at once. First, 安全 is both 'safety' and 'security' — including national security — so 'secure and controllable' and 'safe and controllable' are both defensible and neither is right. Second, 可控 is undifferentiated between (a) controllable by us rather than by a foreign party, (b) socially manageable / not destabilising, and (c) technically controllable, i.e. the alignment property. An English reader who meets 'controllable AI' in a translated PRC document will default to (c); across the corpus, (a) and (b) are at least as common. Compare the 14th Five-Year Plan's 推进金融业信息化核心技术安全可控 — unambiguously sense (a), about not depending on foreign financial IT — with the 2017 AI Plan's 确保把人工智能发展规制在安全可控范围内, which sits in a passage about employment effects and social ethics and is therefore sense (b). The 2025 AI+ Opinions place 安全可控 in a list of governing principles beside 开放共享 (openness and sharing), where it functions as the counterweight to openness rather than as a technical property at all. TC260's AI Safety Governance Framework 2.0 (2025) uses 安全可控环境 for a regulatory sandbox — sense (b) again — while elsewhere in the same document 安全、可靠、可控 carries sense (c). Do not assume the alignment reading without checking what the phrase modifies.

definition_en: The PRC's pre-launch review requirement for internet services with public-opinion attributes or social-mobilisation capacity, extended to generative AI by Article 17 of the 2023 Interim Measures. It runs alongside, and is legally distinct from, algorithm filing.
definition_zh: 中国对具有舆论属性或社会动员能力的互联网服务设定的上线前评估要求，2023 年《生成式人工智能服务管理暂行办法》第十七条将其扩展至生成式人工智能服务。它与算法备案并行，法律性质不同。
pitfalls: A textbook 安全 ambiguity. In the PRC regulatory sense, 安全评估 means a *security/content* assessment tied to public-opinion and social-mobilisation attributes — closer to a content-and-information-security review than to what AI-safety researchers mean by a safety evaluation. Meanwhile in the technical register the same two characters cover capability and risk evaluation: TC260 uses 安全评估测试 for periodic testing, and the field's usual word for model evaluation is 测评 or 评测. So the same phrase can denote a regulatory filing step or a red-teaming exercise. Disambiguate: 上线前安全评估 for the regulatory step, 安全测评 / 风险评测 for technical evaluation.

definition_en: In PRC internet regulation, a named administrative procedure — not the generic English phrase — established by the 2018 Provisions on the Security Assessment of Internet Information Services Having Public Opinion Attributes or Social Mobilisation Capability. It is triggered by five enumerated events (launching such a service or adding such a function; adopting new technologies or applications that materially change the service's public-opinion or mobilisation profile; a marked increase in user numbers producing the same effect; the spread of illegal or harmful information showing existing controls are inadequate; or written notice from a prefecture-level-or-above cyberspace or public security authority). The provider conducts the assessment itself or engages a third party, is answerable for the result, and submits a report through the National Internet Security Management Service Platform to the local cyberspace administration and public security organs, who review it on paper and may follow up with on-site inspection.
definition_zh: 指《具有舆论属性或社会动员能力的互联网信息服务安全评估规定》确立的特定行政程序，而非泛指的"安全性评价"。触发情形有五类：信息服务上线或增设相关功能；使用新技术新应用导致舆论属性或社会动员能力发生重大变化；用户规模显著增加导致同样变化；发生违法有害信息传播扩散；以及地市级以上网信部门或公安机关书面通知。服务提供者自行或委托第三方开展评估并对结果负责，通过全国互联网安全管理服务平台向所在地网信部门和公安机关提交安全评估报告，由其书面审查，必要时开展现场检查。
pitfalls: Three traps. (1) 安全 here is security, not safety: the assessment's enumerated contents are real-name verification, log retention, illegal-information disposal, and channels for supplying technical and data assistance to cyberspace, public security and state security organs — it is not a model-capability or harm evaluation. An English reader who sees 'safety assessment' next to a Chinese AI service will import the wrong content entirely. (2) It is a proper noun for a specific filing procedure; the same two characters also appear in Chinese texts as ordinary English 'security evaluation', and only context distinguishes them. (3) It is a *self*-assessment reviewed on paper, so 'assessment' can sound more independent than it is — but unlike 备案, it must be completed and submitted *before* launch for the first two triggers, which is where the regime's real pre-market gate sits. Coverage that treats 备案 as the gate and 安全评估 as a formality has it exactly backwards.

alt_zh: 权重外泄 / 自我渗出 / 自我逃逸
definition_en: A model copying its own weights out of the environment its operators control, to a machine they do not control. A named capability threshold in several frontier safety frameworks and a precondition for autonomous replication in the wild.
definition_zh: 模型把自己的权重从运营方控制的环境里复制出去，转移到运营方管不到的机器上。多个前沿安全框架把它列为能力阈值，也是 AI 在野外自主复制的前提。
pitfalls: GENUINELY CONTESTED — and the deeper problem is that Chinese discourse mostly does not distinguish this from 自我复制 (self-replication) at all.
